days.label: Day 01
days.title: Nanyuki to Gathiuru to Giant Bamboo Forest Camp
paragraphs: Meet at the Mohakin Mountain Store office in Nanyuki at 11:00 am for a mountain gear and equipment check. The guide will ensure that all essential equipment is available before the trek begins. Meet the mountain team, including the guide, cook and porters, before starting the approximately 17 km drive to Gathiuru Forest Station at 2,300 m. A picnic lunch will be served at the forest station before completing the park registration and entry procedures. After signing into the park, begin the day’s trek of approximately 10 km to the Giant Bamboo Forest Camp at 2,800 m. The trail takes approximately 3–4 hours and follows a beautiful route beneath the canopy of the bamboo forest all the way to camp. Arrive at camp in time for the traditional 4:00 pm tea, coffee and hot drinking chocolate, served with cookies and popcorn. In the evening, enjoy a bonfire while dinner is prepared and served, followed by a peaceful night in 4-season-rated mountain tents with foam mattresses. Overnight: Giant Bamboo Forest Camp.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Giant Bamboo Forest Camp to Highlands Castle Camp
paragraphs: Wake up at 6:00 am and enjoy breakfast at 7:00 am. Be ready to begin trekking by 8:00 am. The day’s trek initially continues for approximately 4 km beneath the bamboo forest canopy. The trail then gradually enters the moorland vegetation zone, covering the remaining approximately 8 km toward the Highlands Castle Camp. Enjoy a hot lunch break along the route before continuing to the camp at approximately 3,559 m. Arrive at camp in time for the 4:00 pm tea, coffee and hot drinking chocolate, served with cookies and popcorn. For smaller groups, there may also be an opportunity to experience the unique possibility of sleeping in a natural mountain cave, depending on the time of the year. Later, enjoy dinner before settling in for the night in 4-season-rated mountain tents with foam mattresses. Overnight: Highlands Castle Camp.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Highlands Castle Camp to American Camp
paragraphs: Wake up at 7:00 am and enjoy breakfast at 7:30 am. Prepare to begin the day’s trek by 8:30 am. Today’s trek takes you higher into the alpine zone, with the objective of reaching American Camp at approximately 4,400 m. Along the way, enjoy a hot lunch break at Two Turn, near the mountain lake, before continuing toward camp. The American Camp is located close to the main peaks of Mount Kenya and offers a spectacular high-altitude environment with beautiful surrounding scenery. Arrive at camp and spend the afternoon resting and acclimatizing in preparation for the early-morning summit attempt. At 4:00 pm, enjoy tea, coffee and hot drinking chocolate served with cookies and popcorn. Dinner will be served later in the evening, followed by an early rest in preparation for the summit trek. Overnight: American Camp.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: American Camp – Point Lenana – Lake Michaelson
paragraphs: Cold desert to alpine and moorland

Wake up at 1:00 am for a light breakfast and prepare for the summit attempt. Begin the approximately 4 km ascent to Point Lenana at 2:00 am, following the trail via Austrian Hut. The route enters the high-altitude cold desert zone as you make your way toward the summit. Reach Point Lenana at 4,985 m in time to witness the spectacular Mount Kenya sunrise, expected between approximately 6:00 and 6:40 am, depending on the time of the year. Celebrate the achievement, take photographs and enjoy the incredible views from the summit. After the summit experience, descend back to Austrian Hut for a full breakfast and a short rest. Later, continue the descent for approximately 5 km to Lake Michaelson at 4,000 m. Lake Michaelson is one of the most spectacular mountain lakes on Mount Kenya, situated on the floor of the magnificent Gorges Valley. The lake is surrounded by a combination of alpine vegetation and moorland grass, creating a dramatic and beautiful high-altitude landscape. A hot lunch will be served upon arrival. Spend the afternoon relaxing around the lake, with the opportunity for trout fishing or a walk around Lake Michaelson, depending on weather conditions and arrangements. Enjoy the 4:00 pm tea, coffee and hot drinking chocolate served with cookies. Dinner will follow, before another night in 4-season-rated mountain tents with foam mattresses. Overnight: Lake Michaelson Camp.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Lake Michaelson – Roadhead – Nithi Waterfalls – Anabas Camp
paragraphs: Begin the day’s trek with a 2.5 km climb out of the Gorges Valley. Once you reach the top of the valley, take time to appreciate the remarkable views toward the eastern side of Mount Kenya. From the top of the valley, continue along the trail toward the roadhead at approximately 3,300 m. This section involves a continuous 8 km descent. Enjoy a hot lunch at the roadhead followed by a short rest. Later, visit the nearby Nithi Waterfalls as you continue the descent for approximately 7 km toward Anabas Campsite. Arrive at camp in time for the 4:00 pm tea, coffee and hot drinking chocolate served with cookies. Enjoy dinner and spend the night in 4-season-rated mountain tents with foam mattresses. Overnight: Anabas Campsite.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Anabas Camp – Clearing Pick-Up Point – Chogoria Forest Gate
paragraphs: Wake up at 7:00 am and have a light breakfast before taking a short walk to nearby water points and designated viewpoints, where there may be opportunities to observe wildlife. Return to camp for a full breakfast at approximately 8:30 am. After breakfast, prepare for the final trek of approximately 10 km to the Clearing pick-up point at 2,500 m. This section descends from the treeline through the bamboo forest and into the upper mountain forest vegetation zone. At the Clearing pick-up point, board the waiting transport for the drive down to the Chogoria Forest Gate at approximately 2,400 m. Complete the park exit procedures and sign out of the park.

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: This 6-day, 5-night Mount Kenya trek combines the remote and scenic Burguret Route on the ascent with the beautiful Chogoria Route on the descent. The trek reaches Point Lenana at 4,985 metres, the highest trekking summit on Mount Kenya, with a sunrise summit attempt before descending through the starting point of the spectacular Gorges Valley into Lake Michaelson Camp.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Chogoria Town – Chogoria Forest Gate – Bandas Camp
paragraphs: Arrival in Chogoria Town is scheduled before or by 12:00 noon. The day begins with a final mountain gear and equipment check to ensure that everything required for the trek is ready. After the equipment check, you will meet the mountain team, including your guide, cook, and porters, before starting the trek toward Mount Kenya. A short vehicle transfer of approximately 20 minutes takes you to the Chogoria Forest Gate, where park entry payments, registration, and other entry formalities are completed. From the forest gate, the vehicle continues for approximately 10 km through the beautiful mountain forest to the trekking starting point at around 2,400 m. After enjoying a picnic lunch, the trek begins. The approximately 10 km trail gradually climbs through the mountain forest toward the treeline at approximately 2,950 m. The walk takes around 4 hours, with the landscape and vegetation changing gradually as altitude is gained. Arrival at Bandas Camp is expected in the afternoon, in time for the traditional 4:00 pm tea, coffee, and cookies. After refreshments, there is an opportunity to take a short walk around the camp and explore the surrounding area, including nearby wildlife water points. Dinner is served at camp, followed by an overnight stay at Bandas Camp.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Bandas Camp to Lake Ellis via Nithi Waterfalls
paragraphs: Breakfast is served at 7:00 am, with the day’s trek beginning at approximately 8:00 am. The trail continues through the spectacular upper mountain environment toward Lake Ellis at 3,450 m, passing through the heather zone and open moorland. The route heads toward the impressive Nithi Waterfalls, providing beautiful scenery and an opportunity to experience the changing landscape as the elevation increases. The trek continues toward the roadhead at approximately 3,300 m, where a hot lunch is served. After lunch and a short rest, the final section of the day’s trek continues toward Lake Ellis. The approximately 13 km journey brings you to Lake Ellis Camp at around 3,450 m. Arrival is expected at approximately 3:00 pm, leaving time to relax and enjoy the peaceful surroundings of the lake. Depending on weather and local conditions, the afternoon can be spent trout fishing in the lake or taking a leisurely walk around the tarn while enjoying the surrounding mountain scenery.At 4:00 pm, tea, coffee, and cookies are served at camp. Dinner follows later in the evening, with an overnight stay at Lake Ellis.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Lake Ellis to Lake Michaelson
paragraphs: Breakfast is served at 7:00 am, with departure scheduled for approximately 8:00 am. The day’s trek continues deeper into the spectacular upper mountain environment toward Lake Michaelson at approximately 4,100 m. The approximately 12 km route takes around 7 hours and passes through the upper moorland and alpine landscape. The trail gradually climbs toward the Gorges Valley, with increasingly dramatic views of the surrounding cliffs, valleys, tarns, and mountain peaks. A lunch break is taken at the Gorges Valley viewpoint at approximately 4,200 m. From this high viewpoint, you can enjoy panoramic views across the magnificent valley and surrounding mountain landscape. After lunch, the trail descends into the floor of the Gorges Valley, eventually reaching the spectacular Lake Michaelson. Surrounded by dramatic cliffs and alpine scenery, the lake is one of the highlights of the Chogoria Route. After arrival, there is time for a short rest before taking a walk toward the shores of Lake Michaelson. Depending on weather conditions, you can enjoy the scenery, take photographs, or try some trout fishing. The surrounding alpine landscape provides an excellent opportunity to appreciate the unique environment of Mount Kenya at high altitude. At 4:00 pm, tea, coffee, and cookies are served at camp. Dinner follows, with an overnight stay near Lake Michaelson.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Lake Michaelson to Upper Simba Tarn (Acclimatization Day)
paragraphs: The trail continues upward toward Upper Simba Tarn at approximately 4,600 m. The approximately 6 km ascent takes around 5 hours as the landscape changes into the cold, rugged alpine and high-altitude desert environment. As the elevation increases, vegetation becomes increasingly sparse and the terrain more dramatic. The route provides impressive views of the surrounding peaks, tarns, and high mountain landscape. Upon arrival at Upper Simba Tarn Camp, a hot lunch is served, followed by a short rest. In the afternoon, an acclimatization trek is undertaken, ascending to approximately 4,700 m before returning to camp. This gradual exposure to higher altitude helps the body adjust before the summit attempt. The remainder of the afternoon is spent resting and preparing for the early morning summit ascent. An early dinner is served, followed by an overnight stay at Upper Simba Tarn Camp.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Point Lenana to Shipton's Camp
paragraphs: Summit day begins at approximately 3:00 am with a light breakfast consisting of tea, hot drinking chocolate, and cookies. After final preparations, the summit trek begins at approximately 4:00 am. The approximately 2.5 km ascent toward Point Lenana at 4,985 m takes around 2.5 hours. The goal is to reach Point Lenana between approximately 6:00 and 6:30 am, in time to witness the sunrise from the highest trekking summit on Mount Kenya. As daylight breaks over the surrounding peaks and valleys, Point Lenana provides spectacular panoramic views across the mountain and, on a clear morning, toward the surrounding landscapes. Time is allowed at the summit to celebrate the achievement, take photographs, and enjoy the incredible high-altitude scenery before beginning the descent. The trail then descends approximately 2 km toward Shipton’s Camp at 4,200 m. On arrival, a full breakfast is served, followed by a well-earned rest. A hot lunch is served later in the day. The afternoon is dedicated to relaxation and recovery after the summit attempt. At approximately 4:00 pm, tea, coffee, and cookies are served at camp. Dinner follows in the evening, with an overnight stay at Shipton’s Camp.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Shipton's Camp to Likii North Camp
paragraphs: Breakfast is served at approximately 7:30 am, followed by the start of the descent at around 8:30 am. The trail descends approximately 10 km toward Likii North Camp at around 3,990 m. As the elevation decreases, the landscape gradually transitions from the high alpine environment into the moorland zone. The descent offers changing views of Mount Kenya’s distinctive vegetation and rugged terrain, with the surrounding landscape becoming increasingly open as altitude is lost. Upon arrival at Likii North Camp, a hot lunch is served, followed by time to rest and recover. In the afternoon, there is an opportunity to take short walks around the camp and enjoy the surrounding mountain environment. At 4:00 pm, tea, coffee, and cookies are served. Dinner follows later in the evening, with an overnight stay at Likii North Camp.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Likii North Camp to Sirimon Gate to Nanyuki
paragraphs: Breakfast is served at 7:00 am, followed by the final trek beginning at approximately 8:00 am. The trail descends approximately 10 km toward Old Moses Camp at around 3,300 m. The descent gradually moves through the moorland toward lower elevations, with the landscape opening up as the mountain environment gives way to broader views of the surrounding countryside. This section of the route provides wide and impressive views across the Laikipia savannah and surrounding rangelands. On a clear day, the expansive landscape provides a memorable final perspective of Mount Kenya. Upon reaching Old Moses Camp, you will board the waiting transport for the approximately 10 km drive down to Sirimon Gate at 2,650 m. At Sirimon Gate, the Mount Kenya National Park exit formalities are completed before saying goodbye to the mountain team. From the gate, you continue by road toward Nanyuki or onward to your next destination. End of Trek

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: This 7-day, 6-night Mount Kenya trek follows the spectacular Chogoria Route for the ascent and descends via the Sirimon Route. The journey takes you through beautiful mountain forests, open moorlands, dramatic valleys, alpine vegetation, and high-altitude landscapes before reaching Point Lenana (4,985 m), the highest trekking summit on Mount Kenya. The trek provides excellent opportunities for acclimatization, with overnight stays at progressively higher elevations and dedicated acclimatization walks before the summit attempt. Along the way, the route passes through scenic highlights including Nithi Waterfalls, Lake Ellis, Gorges Valley, Lake Michaelson, and the alpine tarns surrounding the main peaks. All mountain equipment, camping supplies, food, hiking gear, porters, cook, and guide services should be arranged and prepared before entering the park.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Chogoria Town – Chogoria Gate – Anabas Camp
paragraphs: Arrive in Chogoria Town (2,100 m) before 12:00 noon, with everything required for the trek prepared and ready. After completing the final preparations, we board a vehicle and drive to the Chogoria lower gate, where we complete park registration and entry formalities. From the gate, we continue by vehicle to approximately the 10 km mark at 2,550 m, where the trek begins. After a picnic lunch, we set off on foot through the beautiful mountain forest. The trail gradually climbs for approximately 10 km, taking us through the forest toward the treeline at around 2,950 m, where we reach Anabas Campsite. Upon arrival, we set up camp and have time to relax and enjoy the surroundings. In the evening, dinner will be served around the campfire before settling in for the night. Overnight: Anabas Campsite Meals: Lunch & Dinner

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Anabas Camp to Lake Ellis via Nithi Waterfalls
paragraphs: Breakfast is served at 7:00 am, and we aim to begin hiking by 8:00 am. Today’s trek takes us deeper into the spectacular upper mountain environment. We hike toward the Nithi Waterfalls, reaching approximately 3,200 m after about 8 km of trekking. The Nithi area offers beautiful scenery and an opportunity to appreciate the changing vegetation as we gain altitude. We then continue to the roadhead at approximately 3,300 m, where we stop for a hot lunch and a short rest. After lunch, we continue for another 4 km toward Lake Ellis (3,450 m), our campsite for the night. We aim to arrive at camp at around 2:00 pm, leaving plenty of time to relax and explore the area. Depending on weather conditions and personal preference, the afternoon can be spent walking around the lake, enjoying the scenery, or trying some trout fishing. Dinner will be served at camp before an overnight stay beside Lake Ellis. Overnight: Lake Ellis Camp meals: Breakfast, Lunch & Dinner

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Lake Ellis to Hall Tarns or Mintos Camp via the Gorges Valley
paragraphs: Heather zone to upper moorland / alpine zone

Breakfast is served at 7:00 am, and we aim to start hiking by 8:30 am. Today’s trek takes us from the heather zone into the upper moorland and alpine environment of Mount Kenya. We hike approximately 12 km, gradually gaining altitude as we approach the spectacular high-altitude landscape surrounding the mountain’s main peaks. One of the highlights of the day is the magnificent Gorges Valley. On a clear day, the valley provides breathtaking views of the surrounding cliffs, lakes, valleys, and mountain peaks. Visibility can sometimes be reduced by mist and changing mountain weather, which is a normal feature of Mount Kenya. Our campsite for the night will be either Hall Tarns or Mintos Camp, at approximately 4,200 m. These camps are ideally located close to the main peaks and offer impressive views of the surrounding gorges, lakes, and alpine landscape. After arriving at camp, we have time to rest, acclimatize, and prepare for the summit attempt the following morning. Dinner will be served early, followed by an early night in preparation for the summit hike. Overnight: Hall Tarns / Mintos Camp Meals: Breakfast, Lunch & Dinner

days.label: Day 04
days.title: : Summit Attempt – Point Lenana – Shipton’s Camp – Likii North
paragraphs: Approximately 7-9 hours including the summit attempt

This is the summit day, and we start very early. At approximately 2:00 am, we wake up for a light breakfast consisting of tea and snacks. After preparing our equipment, we begin the 4.5 km ascent toward Point Lenana, the highest trekking summit on Mount Kenya at 4,985 m. The goal is to reach Point Lenana in time for the spectacular sunrise at around 6:30 am. Standing on the summit as the sun rises over the surrounding landscape is one of the most memorable moments of the trek. We take time to celebrate the achievement, enjoy the views, and take photographs before beginning our descent. We descend approximately 3 km on the Sirimon side toward Shipton’s Camp (4,200 m). Here, we stop for a well-deserved full breakfast and a short rest. After breakfast, we continue our descent toward Likii North Camp (approximately 3,990 m). This section takes us through the fascinating alpine landscape, including the giant Lobelia vegetation characteristic of the high-altitude environment. The distance from Shipton’s Camp to Likii North is approximately 7 km, taking around 4 hours, depending on the pace and trail conditions. Lunch may be served at the camp or along the route, depending on the group’s trekking speed and arrival time. In the evening, we enjoy dinner and a campfire before spending our final night on the mountain. Overnight: Likii North Camp Meals: Breakfast, Lunch & Dinner

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Likii North to Old Moses Camp to Sirimon Gate to Nanyuki
paragraphs: Alpine / heather zone to lower mountain forest

Breakfast is served at 7:00 am, and we begin our final descent at approximately 8:00 am. We trek approximately 8 km toward Old Moses Camp (3,300 m), gradually descending into the lower montane vegetation. On a clear day, this section of the trail offers expansive views across the surrounding landscape, including the Laikipia plains and distant rangelands. Upon reaching Old Moses Camp, we board our waiting transport for the remaining approximately 9 km drive to the Sirimon Gate (2,650 m), where we officially exit Mount Kenya National Park. From Sirimon Gate, we continue by road to Nanyuki, a journey of approximately 40 minutes. Upon arrival in Nanyuki, the trek officially comes to an end. End of Trek Congratulations on completing the Mount Kenya Chogoria–Sirimon Traverse and reaching Point Lenana at 4,985 m!

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: This 5-day, 4-night Mount Kenya trek combines the scenic Chogoria Route for the ascent with the Sirimon Route for the descent. The trek takes you through beautiful montane forests, moorlands, alpine vegetation, spectacular valleys, waterfalls, lakes, and finally to Point Lenana (4,985 m), the highest trekking summit on Mount Kenya.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Naru Moru Town to Met Station Camp
paragraphs: Meet or be in Naro Moru Town at 11:00 am or noon, where the guide will assist with a final mountain equipment and gear check to ensure that you have everything required for the trek. From Naro Moru Town, drive approximately 17 km / 30 minutes to the Naro Moru Park Gate at 2,650 m, located within the montane forest vegetation zone. Meet the mountain team, including the guide, cook and porters, before sitting down for a hot lunch. After lunch, complete the park registration and entry formalities before beginning the day’s trek. Start trekking for approximately 10 km through the mountain forest toward Met Station Camp at 3,040 m, located within the treeline vegetation zone. The trek takes approximately 3–4 hours at a slow and comfortable pace, allowing the body to begin adjusting to the increasing altitude. Arrive at camp in time for the traditional 4:00 pm tea, coffee and hot drinking chocolate, served with cookies and popcorn. Enjoy the evening sundowner before dinner is served. Overnight: Met Station Camp.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Met Station Camp to Mackinder Camp
paragraphs: Wake up at 6:00 am and enjoy breakfast at 7:00 am. Be ready to begin the day’s hike at 8:00 am. Today’s trek covers approximately 10 km from the treeline through the moorland vegetation zone, passing through the famous Vertical Bog, a distinctive feature of the Naro Moru Route. Continue toward Mackinder Camp at approximately 4,300 m, entering the alpine vegetation zone. This day involves an elevation gain of more than 1,200 m, making it important to maintain a slow, steady pace. Taking regular short breaks, drinking plenty of water and allowing the body time to adjust to the altitude is recommended. Enjoy a hot lunch break at the Picnic Rocks lunch point before continuing toward Mackinder Camp. Upon arrival, take a short rest before undertaking an acclimatization hike to approximately 4,400 m, returning to camp afterward. Enjoy the 4:00 pm tea, coffee and hot drinking chocolate served with cookies and popcorn. Dinner will be served later, followed by an overnight stay at camp. Overnight: Mackinder Camp.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Mackinder Camp to Shipton's Camp via the Half Peak Circuit
paragraphs: Wake up at 7:00 am and enjoy breakfast at 7:30 am. Be ready to start trekking by 8:30 am. Today’s trek covers approximately 4.5 km to Shipton’s Camp at 4,200 m through the high-altitude cold desert vegetation zone, bringing you very close to the main peaks of Mount Kenya. The route provides an excellent acclimatization experience because the trail involves gaining and losing elevation throughout the day. The highest point reached during the day’s hike is approximately 4,650 m, before descending to Shipton’s Camp at 4,200 m. Along the route, you will encounter several beautiful high-altitude mountain lakes, including Hut Tarn, Nanyuki Tarn, Emerald Tarn and Polish Man Tarn. You will also have views of the magnificent Hausberg and Oblong Tarn. By the time you reach Shipton’s Camp, you will have covered approximately half of the Peak Circuit Route, a spectacular trekking path that circles the main peaks of Mount Kenya. Arrive at Shipton’s Camp in time for a hot lunch and enjoy a short rest. Later, enjoy the traditional 4:00 pm tea, coffee and hot drinking chocolate, served with cookies and popcorn. An early dinner will be served in preparation for the following day’s early-morning summit attempt. Overnight: Shipton’s Camp.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Shipton's Camp to Point Lenana to Met Station Camp
paragraphs: Wake up at 2:00 am for a light breakfast and prepare for the summit attempt. Begin the ascent toward Point Lenana at 4,985 m, the highest trekking summit on Mount Kenya. The summit trek takes approximately 3–4 hours, with the aim of reaching Point Lenana in time for sunrise, expected between approximately 6:00 and 6:40 am, depending on weather and mountain conditions. Reach the summit and take time to celebrate the achievement, enjoy the spectacular surroundings and capture photographs. After spending time at the summit, begin the approximately 4 km descent toward the southwest side of the mountain, joining the Teleki Valley at Mackinder Camp. A full breakfast will be served at Mackinder Camp, followed by a short rest. Later, continue the descent for approximately 10 km to Met Station Camp at 3,040 m. Stop at the Picnic Rocks for a hot lunch before continuing the descent. Arrive at Met Station Camp in time for the 4:00 pm tea, coffee and hot drinking chocolate, served with cookies and popcorn. Enjoy the sundowner before dinner and an overnight stay at camp. Overnight: Met Station Camp.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Met Station Camp to Naru Moru Town
paragraphs: Wake-up is at approximately 7:00 am, followed by breakfast at 7:30 am. After breakfast, the final section of the trek begins at approximately 8:00 am. The approximately 10 km trail gradually descends through the treeline and mountain forest toward the Naro Moru Park Gate. The early morning descent offers opportunities to see wildlife along the trail, depending on the season and conditions. Upon reaching the park gate, the Mount Kenya National Park exit formalities are completed by signing out of the park. After exiting the park, you say goodbye to the mountain team, including the guide, cook, and porters. Waiting transport then takes you back to Naro Moru Town before continuing onward to your next destination. End of Trek.

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: This 5-day, 4-night Mount Kenya trek follows the Naro Moru Route to Point Lenana, the highest trekking summit on Mount Kenya at 4,985 m. The route provides a gradual progression through the mountain’s distinct vegetation zones, from montane forest and bamboo to moorland, alpine vegetation and the high-altitude cold desert. The itinerary also incorporates acclimatization hikes and a section of the peak circuit, allowing trekkers to experience several of Mount Kenya’s spectacular mountain lakes and valleys before making the early-morning summit attempt.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Naru Moru Town to Met Station Camp
paragraphs: Arrival in Naro Moru Town is scheduled for approximately 11:00 am to 12:00 noon. The trek begins with a mountain equipment and gear check, assisted by the guide, to confirm that all the necessary equipment for the hike is available and ready. A vehicle transfer of approximately 17 km, taking around 30 minutes, follows to the Naro Moru Park Gate at approximately 2,650 m. At the park gate, you meet the mountain team, including the guide, cook, and porters. A hot lunch is served before completing the Mount Kenya National Park registration and entry formalities. After registration, the trek begins through the beautiful mountain forest. The approximately 10 km trail gradually climbs toward Met Station Camp at approximately 3,040 m. The trek takes approximately 3–4 hours and is undertaken at a slow and comfortable pace, allowing trekkers to gradually adapt to the increasing elevation. Arrival at Met Station Camp is expected in the afternoon, in time for the 4:00 pm tea, coffee, and hot drinking chocolate served with cookies and popcorn. There is time to relax and enjoy the mountain surroundings and sundowner before dinner is served. Overnight at Met Station Camp.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Met Station Camp – Naro Moru Vertical Bog – Mackinder Camp
paragraphs: Wake-up is at approximately 6:00 am, with breakfast served at 7:00 am. After breakfast, prepare to begin the day’s trek at approximately 8:00 am. The approximately 10 km trail continues upward from the treeline through the moorland zone toward Mackinder Camp at approximately 4,300 m. One of the major features of this section is the famous Naro Moru Vertical Bog, a wet and challenging section of the route. The trail then continues upward through increasingly high-altitude terrain toward the alpine zone. The elevation gain on this day is more than 1,200 m. It is recommended to maintain a slow pace, take regular breaks, and drink plenty of water throughout the trek to help the body adapt to the increasing altitude. A hot lunch break is taken at the Picnic Rocks lunch point before continuing toward Mackinder Camp. Upon reaching camp, there is time for a short rest before undertaking an acclimatization hike to approximately 4,400 m. After reaching the acclimatization point, the group descends back to camp. At 4:00 pm, tea, coffee, and hot drinking chocolate are served with cookies and popcorn. An early dinner is served in preparation for the early morning summit attempt, followed by an overnight stay at Mackinder Camp.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Mackinder Camp to Point Lenana to Met Station Camp
paragraphs: Summit day begins at approximately 1:00 am with a light breakfast consisting of tea, hot drinking chocolate, and cookies. After final preparations, the summit trek begins at approximately 2:00 am. The approximately 4 km ascent toward Point Lenana at 4,985 m takes around 4 hours at a slow and steady pace. The trail passes through the alpine environment and cold desert as the group gradually climbs toward the summit. The goal is to reach Point Lenana between approximately 6:00 and 6:40 am, in time to witness the sunrise from the highest trekking summit on Mount Kenya. At the summit, there is time to celebrate the achievement, take photographs, and enjoy the spectacular sunrise and panoramic views across the surrounding mountain landscape. After spending time at Point Lenana, the group begins the descent back to Mackinder Camp. A full breakfast is served at Mackinder Camp, followed by a short rest. The trek then continues for approximately 10 km downhill toward Met Station Camp at 3,040 m. A hot lunch break is taken at the Picnic Rocks lunch point before continuing the descent. Arrival at Met Station Camp is expected in the afternoon, in time for the 4:00 pm tea, coffee, and hot drinking chocolate served with cookies and popcorn. The evening provides an opportunity to relax and enjoy the sundowner before the final dinner on the mountain. Having completed a long and demanding summit day, an early night is recommended. Overnight at Met Station Camp.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Met Station Camp – Naro Moru Park Gate – Naro Moru Town
paragraphs: Wake-up is at approximately 7:00 am, followed by breakfast at 7:30 am. After breakfast, the final section of the trek begins at approximately 8:00 am. The approximately 10 km trail gradually descends through the treeline and mountain forest toward the Naro Moru Park Gate. The early morning descent offers opportunities to see wildlife along the trail, depending on the season and conditions. Upon reaching the park gate, the Mount Kenya National Park exit formalities are completed by signing out of the park. After exiting the park, you say goodbye to the mountain team, including the guide, cook, and porters. Waiting transport then takes you back to Naro Moru Town before continuing onward to your next destination. End of Trek.

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: This 4-day, 3-night Mount Kenya trek follows the Naro Moru Route to Point Lenana (4,985 m), the highest trekking summit on Mount Kenya. The route provides a direct and rewarding approach to the mountain, passing through montane forest, the distinctive Naro Moru Vertical Bog, open moorland, alpine terrain, and the cold desert zone before reaching the summit. The itinerary includes an acclimatization hike at Mackinder Camp before the summit attempt. The summit ascent begins in the early morning on Day 3, allowing trekkers to reach Point Lenana in time to experience the spectacular sunrise from the mountain. All mountain equipment, hiking gear, food, camping supplies, porters, cook, and guide services should be arranged and ready before entering the park.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Nanyuki to Sirimon Gate to Old Moses / Judmier's Camp
paragraphs: The trek begins at approximately 12:00 noon from the Mohakin Travel Office in Nanyuki at 1,950 m. Before departure, the guide assists with a final mountain equipment and gear check to ensure that all essential equipment required for the trek is available and ready. A vehicle transfer of approximately 40 minutes takes you from Nanyuki to the Sirimon Gate at approximately 2,650 m. Upon arrival at the gate, a hot lunch is served before completing the Mount Kenya National Park registration and entry formalities. After registration, the trek begins from the mid-mountain forest and gradually climbs toward the Old Moses Camp at approximately 3,300 m. The approximately 9.4 km trail takes around 3–4 hours at a slow and comfortable pace. The route passes through beautiful mountain forest before gradually transitioning toward the heather zone. Along the way, there may be opportunities to spot wildlife, including waterbucks, zebras, and, depending on the season and conditions, occasionally elephants. Arrival at Old Moses / Judmier’s Camp is expected in the afternoon, in time for the 4:00 pm tea, coffee, and hot drinks. There is time to relax and enjoy the surrounding mountain landscape and sundowner before dinner is served. Overnight at Old Moses / Judmier’s Camp.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Old Moses Camp – Shipton’s Camp
paragraphs: Wake-up is at approximately 6:30 am, with breakfast served at 7:00 am. After breakfast,prepare to begin the day’s trek at approximately 8:00 am. The approximately 18 km trail continues upward from the heather zone toward the alpine zone, gradually gaining elevation as the route approaches Shipton’s Camp at approximately 4,200 m. The day’s trek takes approximately 6–7 hours and is undertaken at a steady and manageable pace, allowing regular opportunities to rest, hydrate, and appreciate the changing mountain environment. A lunch break is taken at the Likii North River picnic point, providing an opportunity to rest and refuel before continuing toward the higher elevations. As the trail progresses, the vegetation becomes increasingly sparse and the landscape more rugged, with spectacular views of Mount Kenya’s high-altitude terrain. Arrival at Shipton’s Camp is expected in the afternoon, in time for the 4:00 pm tea, coffee, and hot drinking chocolate. After refreshments, there is an opportunity to take a short walk around the camp and enjoy the dramatic surroundings. An early dinner is served in preparation for the following morning’s summit attempt, followed by an overnight stay at Shipton’s Camp.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Shipton’s Camp – Point Lenana – Upper Simba Tarn – Lake Michaelson
paragraphs: 8-10 hours, including the summit ascent and descent

Summit day begins at approximately 2:00 am with a light breakfast consisting of tea, coffee, and cookies. After final preparations, the summit ascent begins at approximately 2:30 am. The approximately 3 km trail to Point Lenana at 4,985 m takes around 3.5 hours at a slow and steady pace. The ascent passes through the high alpine and cold desert environment. The goal is to reach Point Lenana between approximately 6:00 and 6:30 am, in time to witness the sunrise from the highest trekking summit on Mount Kenya. At the summit, there is time to celebrate the achievement, take photographs, and enjoy the spectacular panoramic views across the mountain and surrounding landscape. After spending time at Point Lenana, the descent begins toward the Chogoria side of Mount Kenya. The trail descends approximately 1 km to Upper Simba Tarn at around 4,500 m, where a full breakfast and short rest are provided. After breakfast, the trek continues for approximately 4 km toward Lake Michaelson at around 4,000 m. Lake Michaelson is one of the most spectacular features of the Chogoria Route, surrounded by dramatic cliffs and magnificent high-altitude scenery. Arrival at camp is expected in time for a hot lunch. The afternoon can be spent relaxing around the lake, taking a walk along its shores, enjoying the scenery, or, depending on weather conditions, trying some trout fishing. Later in the evening, a bonfire provides a relaxing atmosphere before dinner is served. Overnight at Lake Michaelson Camp.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Lake Michaelson – Roadhead – Nithi Waterfalls – Anabas Campsite
paragraphs: Begin the day’s trek with a 2.5 km climb out of the Gorges Valley. Once you reach the top of the valley, take time to appreciate the remarkable views toward the eastern side of Mount Kenya. From the top of the valley, continue along the trail toward the roadhead at approximately 3,300 m. This section involves a continuous 8 km descent. Enjoy a hot lunch at the roadhead followed by a short rest. Later, visit the nearby Nithi Waterfalls as you continue the descent for approximately 7 km toward Anabas Campsite. Arrive at camp in time for the 4:00 pm tea, coffee and hot drinking chocolate served with cookies. Enjoy dinner and spend the night in 4-season-rated mountain tents with foam mattresses. Overnight: Anabas Campsite.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Meru Mount Kenya Camp – Clearing Point – Chogoria Gate – Chogoria Town
paragraphs: Wake up at 7:00 am and have a light breakfast before taking a short walk to nearby water points and designated viewpoints, where there may be opportunities to observe wildlife. Return to camp for a full breakfast at approximately 8:30 am. After breakfast, prepare for the final trek of approximately 10 km to the Clearing pick-up point at 2,500 m. This section descends from the treeline through the bamboo forest and into the upper mountain forest vegetation zone. At the Clearing pick-up point, board the waiting transport for the drive down to the Chogoria Forest Gate at approximately 2,400 m. Complete the park exit procedures and sign out of the park. End of Trek Congratulations on completing the 5 Days / 4 Nights Mount Kenya Sirimon–Chogoria Traverse and reaching Point Lenana at 4,985m

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: This 5-day, 4-night Mount Kenya trek combines the Sirimon Route for the ascent with the scenic Chogoria Route for the descent. The trek passes through mountain forests, heather and moorland zones, alpine landscapes, high-altitude tarns, dramatic valleys, waterfalls, and some of the most spectacular scenery on Mount Kenya. The route provides an excellent opportunity to experience the contrasting landscapes on both sides of the mountain while gradually gaining altitude toward Point Lenana (4,985 m), the highest trekking summit on Mount Kenya. The summit attempt takes place early on Day 3, allowing trekkers to reach Point Lenana in time for sunrise before descending along the Chogoria side. All mountain equipment, hiking gear, food, camping supplies, porters, cook, and guide services should be arranged and prepared before entering the park.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Chogoria Town to Lake Ellis via Anabas Camp and Nithi Waterfalls
paragraphs: Man-made forest / mountain forest to heather and moorland

Arrival in Chogoria Town is scheduled for approximately 9:00 am, where you meet the mountain team, including the guide, cook, and porters. Before starting the trek, the guide will assist in mountain gear and equipment check to ensure that all essential equipment required for the expedition is available and ready. A vehicle transfer then takes you toward the Chogoria Forest Gate. The surrounding lower slopes include areas of man-made forest before transitioning into the natural mountain environment. At the forest gate, park entry registration, payments, and other formalities are completed before continuing higher up the mountain by vehicle. The drive continues toward Anabas Camp at approximately 2,950 m. Depending on the arrival time, an early hot lunch can be served at camp, or a packed hot lunch can be carried and enjoyed later along the route. The trek toward Lake Ellis then begins, passing through the spectacular Nithi Waterfalls at approximately 3,200 m. The waterfalls are one of the major attractions along this section of the Chogoria Route. The route continues toward the roadhead at approximately 3,300 m, which provides an ideal location to stop and enjoy a packed hot lunch while taking in the surrounding mountain scenery. After lunch, the final approximately 3.5 km section continues toward Lake Ellis at approximately 3,450 m. Arrival at camp is expected in the afternoon, in time for the 4:00 pm tea, coffee, and hot drinking chocolate served with cookies and popcorn. The afternoon can be spent enjoying a leisurely walk around the lake or trying your hand at trout fishing while appreciating the peaceful surroundings. Dinner is served later in the evening, followed by an overnight stay in comfortable 4-season-rated mountain tents equipped with foam mattresses.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Lake Ellis to Lake Michaelson via Gorges Valley Viewpoint
paragraphs: Wake-up is at approximately 7:00 am, with breakfast served at 7:30 am. After breakfast, preparations are made for the approximately 12.5 km trek toward Lake Michaelson at approximately 4,100 m. The route provides an excellent acclimatization opportunity as it climbs toward the Gorges Valley viewpoint at approximately 4,300 m. This section follows the “trek high, sleep low” principle, allowing the body to experience a higher elevation before descending to the overnight camp. The trek is undertaken at a slow and steady pace, with regular rest stops and adequate hydration recommended to help the body adapt to the increasing altitude. A packed hot lunch is enjoyed at the viewpoint while taking in panoramic views of the rugged mountain peaks above and the lowlands below. On a clear day, the views from this high point are particularly spectacular. After the viewpoint, the trail descends toward the floor of the magnificent Gorges Valley and continues to Lake Michaelson Camp. Upon arrival, there is time for a short rest before taking a leisurely walk toward the shores of Lake Michaelson. The walk provides an opportunity to enjoy the lake and appreciate the dramatic surrounding landscape. Return to camp for the traditional 4:00 pm tea, coffee, and hot drinking chocolate served with cookies and popcorn. Dinner is served later in the evening, followed by another peaceful night in the mountains.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Lake Michaelson – Full-Day Trout Fishing Expedition
paragraphs: Minimal trekking — a dedicated fishing day at the lake

Day 3 is dedicated entirely to the trout fishing expedition, allowing plenty of time to explore Lake Michaelson and its spectacular surroundings without the pressure of a long trekking day. The day begins at approximately 7:00 am with tea, coffee, hot drinking chocolate, cookies, and fruits served before heading to the lake for the first morning fishing session. After the morning fishing session,return to camp at approximately 9:30 am for a full breakfast and a short break. The expedition then returns to the lake for a lake-circuit walk. This provides an opportunity to combine trout fishing with sightseeing while exploring different sections of the lake and surrounding alpine landscape. Return to camp at approximately 1:00 pm for lunch, followed by a longer rest period until approximately 3:00 pm. In the afternoon, return to the lake for another fishing session and leisurely walk along the shores. As the day comes to an end, return to camp for evening snacks followed by dinner. The evening provides an opportunity to relax and enjoy the peaceful high-altitude surroundings before another overnight stay at Lake Michaelson.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Lake Michaelson to Lake Ellis
paragraphs: Wake-up is at approximately 7:00 am, with breakfast served at 8:00 am. After breakfast,prepare to begin the approximately 12.5 km trek back toward Lake Ellis at 3,450 m. For those who would like additional fishing time, the morning can alternatively begin with approximately two hours at Lake Michaelson before starting the descent. The trek begins by climbing approximately 2.5 km out of the Gorges Valley toward the top of the ridge. On a clear day, this section provides beautiful views back toward Lake Michaelson below. From the ridge, the trail continues with a gradual 10 km descent toward Lake Ellis. Arrival at Lake Ellis Camp is expected in time for a hot lunch, followed by a short rest. The afternoon can be spent relaxing at camp or enjoying another trout fishing session at Lake Ellis for those who wish to continue fishing. At 4:00 pm, tea, coffee, and hot drinking chocolate are served with cookies and popcorn. Dinner follows later in the evening, with an overnight stay at Lake Ellis Camp.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Lake Ellis to Chogoria Town via Anabas Camp
paragraphs: Wake-up is at approximately 7:00 am, followed by breakfast at 8:00 am. After breakfast, the final section of the trek begins with an approximately 8 km descent toward Anabas Campsite. This descent follows a different section of the route, avoiding the roadhead and Nithi Waterfalls route used earlier in the expedition. Upon reaching Anabas Camp, waiting transport is boarded for the approximately 22 km drive toward the Chogoria Forest Gate. At the forest gate, the Mount Kenya National Park exit formalities are completed before saying goodbye to the mountain team, including the guide, cook, and porters. The journey then continues by road to Chogoria Town before proceeding onward to Nairobi or your next destination. End of Expedition

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: A 5-day, 4-night expedition designed for trekkers and fishing enthusiasts alike, exploring two of Mount Kenya's spectacular high-altitude lakes — Lake Ellis and Lake Michaelson. This is not a summit attempt: the itinerary combines scenic mountain trekking with dedicated time for trout fishing, leisurely walks, and acclimatization, with a full day set aside purely for fishing at Lake Michaelson. The route passes through mountain forest, heather and moorland, the dramatic Gorges Valley, and Nithi Waterfalls.

days.title: Mohakin Mountain Store to Sirimon Gate to Old Moses Camp
paragraphs: Meet at Mohakin Mountain Store at noon for a mountain gear and equipment check assisted by the guide. This is also an opportunity to meet the mountain team, including the guide, cook and porters, and make final preparations for the trek. Board the transport and drive for approximately 40 minutes to Sirimon Gate at 2,659 m, located within the mid-mountain forest. Upon arrival, stop for a hot lunch before completing the park entry registration and other required formalities. Begin the trek from the Sirimon Gate area, covering approximately 9 km through the mountain forest toward Old Moses Camp at 3,300 m. As the trail gains elevation, the vegetation gradually changes into the heather zone. Arrive at camp in time for the traditional 4:00 pm tea, coffee and hot drinking chocolate, served with cookies and popcorn. Later, enjoy the mountain sunset and surrounding scenery as dinner is prepared and served. Overnight at Old Moses in either mountain tents or mountain huts, subject to availability.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Old Moses to Shipton's Camp via Likii River
paragraphs: Wake up at approximately 6:00 am and have breakfast at 7:00 am before preparing to start the day’s trek at 8:00 am. Today’s trek covers approximately 18 km toward Shipton’s Camp at 4,200 m, located at the upper end of the Alpine vegetation zone. The trail gradually gains altitude through the changing mountain landscape and offers spectacular views across the northern slopes of Mount Kenya. A packed lunch or hot lunch break is taken at the Likii River lunch point, providing time to rest and refuel before continuing higher. After lunch, the landscape becomes increasingly alpine, with distinctive high-altitude vegetation and rocky terrain creating a dramatic mountain environment. Continue steadily toward Shipton’s Camp, maintaining a comfortable pace to support acclimatization. Arrive at camp in time for the 4:00 pm tea, coffee and hot drinks. Enjoy some time to rest and take in the surrounding alpine scenery before an early dinner and overnight at Shipton’s Camp.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Shipton's Camp to Point Lenana to Mackinder Camp to Met Station
paragraphs: This is the summit day. Wake up at approximately 2:00 am and have a light breakfast before beginning the summit attempt. Start the ascent toward Point Lenana at 4,985 m, covering approximately 3.5 km. The climb takes around 3–4 hours, with the aim of reaching Point Lenana in time for sunrise, usually between 6:00 am and 6:40 am, depending on the time of year and trekking conditions. Reach Point Lenana and take time to enjoy the achievement, capture photographs and appreciate the spectacular sunrise and panoramic views from Mount Kenya’s highest trekking summit. After the summit, descend approximately 3 km toward the south-western side of the mountain and enter the Teleki Valley, continuing to Mackinder’s Camp at 4,300 m. Here, enjoy a full breakfast followed by a short rest. Continue the descent for approximately 10 km toward Met Station Camp at 3,040 m. Take a lunch break at the Picnic Rocks before continuing through the famous Vertical Bog, one of the distinctive sections of the Naro Moru Route. Proceed to Met Station Camp, where an early dinner is served. After the long summit day, rest and recover overnight at camp.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Met Station to Naro Moru Park Gate
paragraphs: Wake up at approximately 7:00 am and have breakfast at 8:00 am before beginning the final section of the trek. Descend approximately 10 km through the mountain forest toward the Naro Moru Park Gate at approximately 2,400 m. As the elevation decreases, the vegetation becomes denser and the mountain environment gradually transitions toward the lower forest. Upon reaching the park gate, complete the exit formalities and conclude the Mount Kenya trek. Meet the transport team for onward travel according to the agreed arrangements. End of Trek Congratulations on completing the Sirimon Route – Point Lenana – Naro Moru Route Mount Kenya trek. The journey combines varied mountain landscapes, challenging high-altitude trekking and the achievement of reaching Point Lenana at 4,985 m.

extraSections.title: Route overview

After the summit, the route descends through the Teleki Valley and the famous vertical bog before reaching Naro Moru Park Gate. Suitable for hikers looking to experience Mount Kenya with time for acclimatization and a gradual approach to the summit.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Nairobi to Masai Mara
paragraphs: Your safari begins with a morning pick-up from your Nairobi hotel at around 8:00 AM. From Nairobi, you will travel through the scenic Great Rift Valley, with a stop at the viewpoint where you can take photographs and enjoy the expansive landscape. Continue towards the Masai Mara, arriving at approximately 1:00 PM. After checking into your accommodation, enjoy lunch before settling in for a short rest. Later in the afternoon, head out for your first game drive in the Masai Mara. As you explore the savannah plains, keep an eye out for some of Kenya’s most iconic wildlife, including lions, elephants, cheetahs and other animals. Return to the camp around 6:30 PM for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Full Day in Masai Mara
paragraphs: Today is dedicated to exploring the Masai Mara. You may begin with an early morning game drive, when wildlife activity is often high, before returning to the lodge for breakfast. Continue with another game drive through the vast savannah plains, exploring different areas of the reserve and looking for the Big Five. The route can include a visit towards the Mara River, where hippos and crocodiles may be seen. Enjoy lunch either at the camp or as a picnic in the reserve, depending on the day’s schedule, before continuing with afternoon game viewing. Return to the camp in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Masai Mara Full Day
paragraphs: Spend another full day exploring the Masai Mara, visiting different areas of the reserve in search of its abundant wildlife. The day provides opportunities to look for cheetahs and leopards, as well as lions, elephants, wildebeest and other species. During the migration season, the Mara River is also an important area to explore as wildebeest move through the ecosystem. Enjoy lunch at the camp or carry a packed lunch for an extended game drive inside the reserve. For those interested, optional experiences such as a hot-air balloon safari at dawn or a Maasai village cultural visit can be arranged. Return to the camp for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Masai Mara to Lake Nakuru
paragraphs: After breakfast, check out and begin your journey towards Lake Nakuru National Park. An optional early morning game drive in the Masai Mara can be arranged before departure, with additional park fees applying. The journey takes you through scenic landscapes, including views around Mount Longonot and Lake Naivasha. Arrive at Lake Nakuru at approximately 3:00 PM and check into your accommodation. Later in the afternoon, head out for a game drive through the park. Lake Nakuru is known for its flamingos, black and white rhinos and opportunities to see tree-climbing lions. Return to the camp in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Lake Nakuru to Lake Naivasha
paragraphs: Lake Naivasha Sopa Resort or similar

Begin the day with an early morning game drive in Lake Nakuru, exploring the park between approximately 6:30 AM and 11:00 AM. Continue searching for black and white rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, buffaloes, leopards and the abundant birdlife around the lake, including flamingos. After the game drive, depart for nearby Lake Naivasha. Check into your accommodation and enjoy lunch before heading out for an afternoon boat safari. The boat ride offers the opportunity to see hippos in the water and a variety of bird species around the lake. An optional visit to Crescent Island can also be arranged, where you can take a walking safari among giraffes, zebras and wildebeest. Return to your accommodation for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Lake Naivasha to Amboseli
paragraphs: Enjoy a relaxed morning at Lake Naivasha, or take part in an optional cycling tour at Hell’s Gate National Park. After breakfast, depart for Amboseli National Park, travelling through the Kenyan countryside and Maasai lands towards the southern part of the country. Arrive in the Amboseli area in the afternoon and continue into the park for your first game viewing experience. Amboseli is particularly known for its large elephant herds and spectacular views of Mount Kilimanjaro. After the afternoon game drive, check into your accommodation, enjoy dinner and settle in for the night.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Full Day Amboseli
paragraphs: Spend a full day discovering Amboseli National Park. Begin with an early morning game drive, when the skies are often clearer and there are opportunities for beautiful views of Mount Kilimanjaro. Explore areas where large elephant herds gather around the park’s wetlands and swamps, while also looking for lions and other wildlife. Visit Observation Hill for panoramic views across the park and its surrounding landscape. Enjoy a picnic lunch in the park before continuing with afternoon game viewing. As the day progresses, explore more of Amboseli’s diverse habitats before returning to your accommodation for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 08
days.title: Amboseli Full Day
paragraphs: Continue exploring Amboseli with another full day of game viewing. Start with an early morning game drive around 6:00 AM, providing an opportunity for sunrise photography and views of Mount Kilimanjaro. After the morning drive, return for breakfast and some time to relax. Later, head out again to explore different areas of the park, including the swamps where elephants gather and the dry lake bed. The varied landscapes provide excellent opportunities for wildlife photography, particularly with Mount Kilimanjaro forming the backdrop. Return to your camp in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 09
days.title: Amboseli to Nairobi
paragraphs: On your final morning, you may take an optional early morning game drive to enjoy one last opportunity to see the sunrise over Mount Kilimanjaro and encounter wildlife in the park. Return to the camp for breakfast before checking out at around 9:00 AM. Begin the drive back to Nairobi, with lunch along the way. Arrive in Nairobi at approximately 2:00–3:00 PM, where you will be dropped off at your hotel or at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for your onward flight.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Full Day Masai Mara
paragraphs: Today is dedicated to exploring the Masai Mara with morning and afternoon game drives. After breakfast, set out into the reserve to search for the Big Five and other wildlife. The game drive may take you towards the Mara River, an important part of the ecosystem where hippos and crocodiles can be seen. Enjoy a picnic lunch in the reserve before continuing with the day’s wildlife exploration. The afternoon provides another opportunity for wildlife photography as you move through different areas of the Mara. Return to your camp in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Masai Mara Game Drives
paragraphs: Continue your exploration of the Masai Mara with another full day of game viewing. The day’s route will take you through different sections of the reserve in search of wildlife, with opportunities to see cheetahs, leopards and other predators, as well as the wider range of animals found across the savannah. For guests interested in additional experiences, an optional hot-air balloon safari can be arranged. A Maasai village visit is also available as an optional cultural experience. Enjoy lunch either at the lodge or as a packed picnic during the game drive before continuing with wildlife viewing. Return to the camp for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Masai Mara to Amboseli
paragraphs: After breakfast, check out and begin the journey from the Masai Mara towards Amboseli National Park. The journey takes you through the changing landscapes of Kenya, including the Great Rift Valley region and Maasai lands. Continue south towards Amboseli, arriving in the late afternoon. After checking in, head out for an evening game drive. As you explore the park, look for elephants and other wildlife while enjoying views of Mount Kilimanjaro when conditions allow. Return to the camp for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Full Day Amboseli
paragraphs: Spend a full day exploring Amboseli National Park. Begin with an early morning game drive, when the conditions may provide some of the best opportunities to see Mount Kilimanjaro. Continue through the park’s wetlands and open plains, where large elephant herds can often be found. Visit Observation Hill for panoramic views across the Amboseli landscape and enjoy a picnic lunch with the mountain forming a spectacular backdrop. Continue with an afternoon game drive through different habitats, including the swamps and dry lake bed, before returning to the lodge in the evening.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Amboseli Game Viewing
paragraphs: Enjoy another full day of wildlife exploration in Amboseli. Begin with an early morning drive for sunrise photography and another opportunity to enjoy views of Mount Kilimanjaro. After returning for breakfast, take some time to relax before heading out again for further game viewing. The afternoon drive allows you to explore more of the park and its different landscapes. Continue looking for elephants and other wildlife while enjoying the dramatic scenery surrounding Amboseli. Return to the camp for your final evening in the park, followed by dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Amboseli to Nairobi
paragraphs: Enjoy an optional early morning game drive for one final opportunity to experience Amboseli and see Mount Kilimanjaro in the morning light. Return to the camp for breakfast and check out at approximately 9:00 AM. Begin your journey back to Nairobi, with lunch at the lodge or as a picnic along the way. Arrive in Nairobi at approximately 2:00–3:00 PM, where you will be dropped off at your hotel or Jomo Kenyatta International Airport.

days.title: Masai Mara Game Viewing
paragraphs: Continue discovering the Masai Mara with another full day of game viewing. Explore different areas of the reserve in search of predators and other wildlife, with opportunities to see cheetahs, leopards and the many species that inhabit the Mara ecosystem. Guests interested in additional experiences may choose an optional hot-air balloon safari or a Maasai village visit. Enjoy lunch at the lodge or carry a packed lunch for a full day inside the reserve before continuing with the afternoon game drive. Return to your accommodation for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Masai Mara to Lake Nakuru
paragraphs: After breakfast, check out and begin the journey from the Masai Mara towards Lake Nakuru National Park. Travel through the changing landscapes of the Great Rift Valley before arriving at Lake Nakuru at approximately 3:00 PM. After checking into your accommodation, head out for an afternoon game drive. Explore the park in search of its well-known wildlife, including black and white rhinos, Rothschild giraffes and other species. The park is also known for its birdlife and flamingos. Return to the camp in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Lake Nakuru Full Day
paragraphs: Today is dedicated to exploring Lake Nakuru National Park. Begin with a game drive through the park, visiting different areas around the lake and its surrounding habitats. Keep watch for black and white rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, buffaloes, leopards and the park’s diverse birdlife. The day also provides opportunities to look for the famous tree-climbing lions found in the area. Enjoy lunch during the day’s activities before continuing with further game viewing and photography. Return to your accommodation in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Lake Nakuru to Nairobi
paragraphs: Enjoy a final morning game drive in Lake Nakuru, providing one last opportunity to explore the park and encounter its wildlife. After the game drive, return for breakfast before beginning the journey back to Nairobi. Lunch will be at the lodge or as a picnic along the way. Arrive in Nairobi at approximately 2:00 PM, where you will be dropped off at your hotel or Jomo Kenyatta International Airport. This marks the end of your safari.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Nairobi to Amboseli
paragraphs: Your safari begins with a morning departure from Nairobi towards Amboseli National Park. Travel through the Kenyan countryside as you make your way towards the park, arriving in time for lunch. After settling into your accommodation, take some time to relax before heading out for your first afternoon game drive. Explore the open plains of Amboseli while enjoying views of Mount Kilimanjaro when conditions allow. The park is particularly known for its large elephant herds and the striking landscape surrounding the mountain. Return to your accommodation in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Full Day Amboseli
paragraphs: Full day exploring Amboseli. Morning drive for Kilimanjaro. Watch elephant herds, visit swamps. Picnic lunch. Overnight.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Amboseli to Tsavo West
paragraphs: After breakfast, begin the journey from Amboseli towards Tsavo West National Park. Continue through the changing landscapes of southern Kenya before entering Tsavo West. One of the highlights of the day is a visit to Mzima Springs, an important water source where you may see hippos and a variety of birdlife. Continue with an afternoon game drive through Tsavo West, exploring the park’s diverse landscapes and searching for wildlife. Return to your accommodation for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Tsavo West Exploration
paragraphs: Today is dedicated to exploring Tsavo West National Park. Enjoy game drives through the park, visiting different habitats and searching for its diverse wildlife. The day may include a visit to the rhino sanctuary and the striking Shetani lava flows. Tsavo West is also known for its distinctive red elephants, which have become one of the area’s most recognizable features. Continue with wildlife viewing and photography before returning to your accommodation for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Tsavo West to Tsavo East
paragraphs: After breakfast, depart Tsavo West and travel towards Tsavo East National Park. Continue with game viewing along the way as you make the transfer between the two parks. Upon arrival in Tsavo East, continue to explore the surrounding landscape before proceeding to your accommodation. Later, visit the area around Aruba Dam, an important water source and wildlife viewing location. Return to your accommodation for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Full Day Tsavo East
paragraphs: Spend a full day exploring Tsavo East National Park. Set out for morning game viewing before continuing with an afternoon drive through the park. Explore the open landscapes and different habitats while searching for elephants and other wildlife. The day also provides opportunities to see the Yatta Plateau and capture photographs of the dramatic scenery and wildlife. Return to the lodge in the evening for dinner and overnight. The day also provides opportunities to see the Yatta Plateau and capture photographs of the dramatic scenery and wildlife. Return to the lodge in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Tsavo East to Nairobi/Mombasa
paragraphs: Begin your final day with a morning game drive through Tsavo East, giving you one last opportunity to experience the park and encounter its wildlife. After the game drive, begin your journey towards your final destination. Depending on your travel arrangements, you may continue to Nairobi or Mombasa, arriving in the afternoon for your hotel or onward travel arrangements. This marks the end of your safari.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Nairobi / Mount Kenya to Samburu
paragraphs: Approx. 6 hours from Nairobi, or approx. 3 hours from the Mount Kenya region

Your safari begins with a morning departure from Nairobi, Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, or your Mount Kenya base town, including Nanyuki, Naro Moru or Chogoria. The drive from Nairobi takes approximately 6 hours, with a lunch stop in Nanyuki, passing scenic views of Kenya's central highlands, coffee and tea plantations, Mount Kenya and the open savannah landscapes of Laikipia. From the Mount Kenya region, the drive takes approximately 3 hours, depending on your starting point, with a lunch stop in Isiolo or at your lodge. Upon arrival in Samburu, check in at your accommodation and enjoy a refreshing fruit juice as you settle in. At 3:00 pm, head out for your first evening game drive until approximately 6:30 pm. Samburu is famous for its unique wildlife, often referred to as the Special Five of Samburu: Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, gerenuk, Beisa oryx and Somali ostrich. You may also encounter elephants, lions, leopards and numerous bird species. Return to your lodge or camp in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Full Day in Samburu National Reserve
paragraphs: Begin the day with a light breakfast at 6:00 am before heading out for an early morning game drive. The cooler morning hours offer excellent opportunities to observe wildlife as animals become active across the reserve. Continue exploring until approximately 10:00 am, then return to camp for a full breakfast and a short rest. After breakfast, you may visit a traditional Samburu manyatta (homestead), offering an opportunity to learn about the local community's culture, traditions and way of life. Return to your accommodation to relax during the warmer midday hours before heading out for an afternoon game drive, exploring different sections of the reserve while searching for wildlife and enjoying the distinctive landscapes of northern Kenya. In the evening, return to camp and enjoy a relaxing campfire and, where available, a barbecue dinner featuring nyama choma before settling in for the night.
- Samburu cultural visit — manyatta homestead tour

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Morning Game Drive & Departure
paragraphs: Return journey — duration depends on destination

Start your final day with a light breakfast at 6:00 am before heading out for an early morning game drive. Explore the reserve during the cooler hours, with another opportunity to spot wildlife, observe birdlife and enjoy the beautiful Samburu landscape. Return to your accommodation at approximately 10:00 am for a full breakfast, followed by check-out. After breakfast, depart Samburu and continue to Nairobi, the Mount Kenya region or your next destination, depending on your travel arrangements. This marks the end of your Samburu wilderness safari.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Moshi/Arusha to Londorossi Gate to Mti Mkubwa Camp
paragraphs: The expedition begins with a final equipment and gear check at your hotel in Moshi or Arusha before driving west toward Londorossi Gate at approximately 2,250 metres. After completing registration and park entry formalities, the trek begins through the dense montane rainforest. The trail climbs steadily through lush vegetation, with tall trees, moss-covered surroundings and giant ferns creating a cool forest environment. You may also hear or spot colobus monkeys in the canopy. The trek continues toward Mti Mkubwa Camp at approximately 2,850 metres, where you will have dinner and settle in for your first night on the mountain.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Mti Mkubwa to Shira 1 Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave the rainforest behind as the trail climbs toward the vast Shira Plateau. The vegetation gradually changes into heather and moorland, opening up to expansive views across the western side of Kilimanjaro. As you gain elevation, the snow-capped summit of Kibo becomes increasingly prominent above the plateau. You will continue toward Shira 1 Camp at approximately 3,610 metres, where you will have time to rest and enjoy the open mountain landscape before dinner.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Shira 1 to Shira 2 Camp
paragraphs: Today’s trek is deliberately gentle, giving your body additional time to adjust to the increasing altitude. You continue across the open Shira Plateau, following a gradual trail toward Shira 2 Camp at approximately 3,850 metres. The wide plateau provides impressive views of the surrounding volcanic landscape and Kibo. Upon arrival at camp, you will have time to rest and, depending on weather conditions, undertake a short acclimatization walk before returning to camp for dinner.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Shira 2 to Moir Hut
paragraphs: Today the route begins its transition toward the remote northern side of Kilimanjaro. Leaving the main Shira trail, you head north around the western flank of Kibo, moving away from the busier southern circuit. The landscape becomes increasingly volcanic and barren as you enter the alpine desert zone. You will continue toward Moir Hut at approximately 4,200 metres, a remote camp surrounded by dramatic volcanic terrain and expansive views. After arriving, you will have time to rest and enjoy dinner in the quiet mountain environment.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Moir Hut to Buffalo Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you continue the gradual circumnavigation of Kilimanjaro along the northern slopes. The trail passes through increasingly remote volcanic terrain, with broad views toward the northern plains and the Kenyan side of the mountain. Although you remain at high altitude, the day’s route has a slight net descent, providing valuable time for continued acclimatization. You will arrive at Buffalo Camp at approximately 4,020 metres, where you will have dinner and rest.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Buffalo Camp to Third Cave
paragraphs: Today’s trek is relatively gentle, with the trail continuing around the northern slopes of Kilimanjaro. The route follows the high-altitude landscape beneath the northern side of Kibo before gradually descending toward Third Cave Camp at approximately 3,870 metres. This slight descent provides another opportunity for your body to consolidate the altitude gained during the preceding days. After arriving at camp, you will have time to rest, enjoy dinner and prepare for the final approach toward the summit.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Third Cave to School Hut
paragraphs: After breakfast, you begin the short but steady ascent toward School Hut at approximately 4,750 metres. The landscape becomes increasingly barren as you approach the upper slopes of Kibo. Because the summit attempt will begin around midnight, today’s trek is deliberately kept short to allow plenty of time for rest and preparation. Upon arrival at School Hut, you will have time to settle in while your guide conducts a final summit briefing and equipment check. An early dinner will be served before you rest in preparation for the summit ascent.

days.label: Day 08
days.title: School Hut to Uhuru Peak to Mweka Camp
paragraphs: You begin the day with an ascent toward the upper slopes of Kibo and the Northern Crater, one of the least-visited areas of Mount Kilimanjaro. The Northern Crater provides a rare opportunity to experience a remote section of the mountain away from the main trekking routes. The stark volcanic landscape, crater walls and surrounding ice fields create a dramatic high-altitude environment. From the crater area, the route continues toward Uhuru Peak at 5,895 metres. UHURU PEAK – 5,895 M After reaching the summit, you will have time to celebrate your achievement and take photographs before descending back toward the crater area. You will spend the night at Crater Camp, subject to route and mountain conditions, providing a unique opportunity to experience the high-altitude crater environment.

days.label: Day 09
days.title: Mweka Camp to Mweka Gate to Moshi/Arusha
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave the high-altitude crater environment and begin the long descent toward the southern slopes of Kilimanjaro. The route descends through the arctic and alpine desert zones, gradually reaching moorland before continuing toward the lower slopes. As the altitude decreases, vegetation becomes increasingly abundant and the environment becomes warmer. You will continue toward Mweka Camp at approximately 3,100 metres, where you will have dinner and rest after the demanding summit and descent stages.

days.label: Day 10
days.title: Rest Day in Moshi/Arusha
paragraphs: After breakfast, you begin the final descent through the lush montane rainforest toward Mweka Gate. The trail gradually descends through the forest, bringing you back into the warmer environment of the lower slopes. Upon reaching Mweka Gate, you will complete the park exit procedures and receive your Kilimanjaro summit certificate. You will then meet your vehicle for the transfer back to Moshi or Arusha, where you can check into your hotel, enjoy a hot shower and relax after completing the Northern Crater Kilimanjaro expedition.

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: The Northern Crater Route is an exceptional Mount Kilimanjaro experience combining gradual acclimatization, remote landscapes and a rarely visited section of the mountain. Beginning on the western side of Kilimanjaro, the route crosses the spectacular Shira Plateau before turning north around Kibo. The northern slopes are considerably quieter than the main southern circuit, offering a more secluded trekking experience with expansive views of the mountain and surrounding landscapes. The route also visits the Northern Crater, one of the least-visited areas of Kilimanjaro, before continuing toward the summit. With several days spent at progressively higher elevations and additional time for acclimatization, this itinerary provides a gradual approach to Uhuru Peak at 5,895 metres. After the summit, the descent follows the Mweka Route through the southern slopes of Kilimanjaro.
