paragraphs: After breakfast at your hotel, you will meet your guide for a final equipment and gear check before beginning the drive west toward Londorossi Gate at approximately 2,250 metres. After completing registration and park entry procedures, the trek begins through the dense montane rainforest. The trail climbs gradually beneath tall trees and lush vegetation, with the possibility of seeing colobus monkeys and other forest wildlife along the way. You will continue toward Mti Mkubwa Camp at approximately 2,850 metres, where you will have dinner and settle in for your first night on the mountain.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Mti Mkubwa to Shira 1 Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave the rainforest behind as the trail climbs toward the vast Shira Plateau. The vegetation gradually changes to open heather and moorland, creating wide views across the western side of Kilimanjaro. As you gain elevation, Kibo’s snow-capped summit becomes increasingly prominent. You will continue to Shira 1 Camp at approximately 3,610 metres, where you will have time to rest and enjoy the open mountain landscape before dinner.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Shira 1 to Shira 2 Camp
paragraphs: Today’s trek is deliberately paced to allow your body additional time to adjust to the altitude. You continue across the broad and open Shira Plateau, with the trail gradually gaining elevation toward Shira 2 Camp at approximately 3,850 metres. The relatively gentle terrain provides an opportunity to enjoy the surrounding volcanic landscape while continuing the acclimatization process. Upon arrival at camp, you will have time to rest. Depending on weather conditions, your guide may recommend a short acclimatization walk before returning to camp for dinner and an overnight rest.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Shira 2 to Moir Hut
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave the main Shira trail and begin heading north around the western and northern slopes of Kibo. As you move farther from the main routes, the landscape becomes increasingly remote and volcanic, with fewer trekkers along the trail. The route continues through the alpine desert zone toward Moir Hut at approximately 4,200 metres. The day’s gradual altitude gain provides another opportunity for acclimatization while you experience the quieter northern side of Kilimanjaro. After arriving at Moir Hut, you will have time to rest and enjoy dinner in the remote mountain environment.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Moir Hut to Buffalo Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you continue the circumnavigation of Kilimanjaro along the remote northern slopes. The trail traverses the high-altitude landscape beneath the northern side of Kibo, with dramatic views across the mountain and the surrounding landscapes. Although you remain at high altitude, the day’s route has a gentle net descent, giving your body further opportunity to adapt before the summit approach. You will arrive at Buffalo Camp at approximately 4,020 metres, where you will have dinner and rest.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Buffalo Camp to Third Cave
paragraphs: After breakfast, you continue along the northern circuit beneath the slopes of Kibo. The trail gradually descends through the alpine desert, providing another relatively gentle day that supports the ongoing acclimatization process. You will continue toward Third Cave Camp at approximately 3,870 metres. Upon arrival, you will have time to rest and recover while preparing for the final approach toward the summit camp. Dinner will be served at camp before an overnight rest.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Third Cave to School Hut
paragraphs: After breakfast, you begin the relatively short ascent toward School Hut at approximately 4,750 metres. The trail continues through the high alpine desert as you approach the eastern side of Kibo. Because the summit attempt begins around midnight, the day is deliberately kept short to allow plenty of time for rest. Upon arrival at School Hut, you will have lunch before resting and preparing your summit equipment. Your guide will conduct a final summit briefing and equipment check, ensuring you are ready for the overnight ascent. An early dinner will be served before you rest for several hours in preparation for the summit climb.

days.label: Day 08
days.title: School Hut to Uhuru Peak to Mweka Camp
paragraphs: You will wake around midnight and begin the final ascent toward Uhuru Peak, the highest point of Mount Kilimanjaro and the highest point in Africa. The climb begins in darkness as you ascend slowly over volcanic scree toward the crater rim. Your guide will maintain a steady pace to help conserve energy and manage the effects of altitude. As dawn approaches, you will continue toward Uhuru Peak at 5,895 metres. UHURU PEAK – 5,895 M After reaching the summit, you will have time to celebrate your achievement and take photographs before beginning the long descent. The route descends toward the lower slopes before continuing through the changing ecological zones toward Mweka Camp at approximately 3,100 metres. The descent from the summit is long, but the lower elevation provides welcome relief after the high-altitude climb. Upon arriving at Mweka Camp, you will have dinner and a well-earned rest.

days.label: Day 09
days.title: Mweka Camp to Mweka Gate to Moshi/Arusha
paragraphs: After breakfast, you begin the final descent through the lush montane rainforest toward Mweka Gate. The trail gradually descends through the forest, bringing you back into warmer and denser vegetation. Upon reaching Mweka Gate, you will complete the park exit procedures and receive your Kilimanjaro summit certificate. You will then meet your vehicle for the transfer back to Moshi or Arusha, where you can check into your hotel, enjoy a hot shower and relax after completing your Kilimanjaro adventure.

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: The Northern Circuit Route is the longest standard route on Mount Kilimanjaro and offers one of the mountain’s most comprehensive trekking experiences. The route begins on the western side of Kilimanjaro before crossing the Shira Plateau and continuing around the quiet northern slopes. With more time spent on the mountain, the route provides an excellent opportunity for gradual acclimatization. It also offers a quieter experience away from the busier southern trails, with spectacular views of Kilimanjaro from different sides. The route eventually joins the eastern side of the mountain before approaching the summit through School Hut. After reaching Uhuru Peak at 5,895 metres, the descent follows the Mweka Route through the southern slopes.

Upon arrival at camp, you will have time to settle in, enjoy dinner and rest before the following day’s trek.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Mti Mkubwa to Shira 1 Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave the rainforest behind and continue climbing toward the vast Shira Plateau. As the vegetation becomes lower and more open, the landscape changes into moorland, with expansive views across the western side of Kilimanjaro. You will continue toward Shira 1 Camp at approximately 3,610 metres, where you may have your first clear views of Kibo, the highest volcanic cone of Kilimanjaro. After arriving at camp, you will have time to rest and enjoy the spectacular high-altitude surroundings before dinner.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Shira 1 to Shira 2 Camp
paragraphs: Today’s trek is deliberately paced to give your body additional time to acclimatize to the increasing altitude. You continue across the open Shira Plateau, with views toward Kibo and the surrounding volcanic landscape. The trail gradually gains elevation toward Shira 2 Camp at approximately 3,850 metres. Upon arrival, you will have time to rest. Depending on weather conditions and how the group is feeling, your guide may recommend a short acclimatization walk before returning to camp. Dinner will be served before an overnight rest.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: – SHIRA 2 CAMP TO LAVA TOWER TO BARRANCO CAMP
paragraphs: Today is an important acclimatization day following the principle of “climb high, sleep low.” You leave Shira 2 Camp and gradually ascend toward Lava Tower at approximately 4,600 metres. The landscape becomes increasingly barren as you enter the alpine desert zone. After reaching Lava Tower, you begin descending toward the spectacular Barranco Valley. The descent allows you to sleep at a lower elevation than the highest point reached during the day, helping your body adapt to the altitude. You will arrive at Barranco Camp at approximately 3,960 metres, situated beneath the impressive Barranco Wall and surrounded by dramatic mountain scenery. After dinner, you will rest at camp in preparation for the following day’s trek.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Barranco to Karanga Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you begin the ascent of the famous Barranco Wall. The climb involves scrambling over sections of rock and using your hands for balance in places. It is non-technical and does not require specialist climbing equipment. After reaching the top of the wall, the trail continues across a series of ridges and valleys toward Karanga Camp at approximately 4,035 metres. Although the day’s distance is relatively short, the terrain provides a good physical challenge while allowing continued acclimatization. After arriving at camp, you will have time to rest and prepare for the ascent toward Barafu Camp.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Karanga to Barafu Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave Karanga Camp and continue toward Barafu Camp at approximately 4,673 metres, the main base camp for the summit attempt. The landscape becomes increasingly barren as you climb deeper into the alpine desert zone. The distance is relatively short, but the significant altitude gain requires a slow and steady pace. Upon reaching Barafu Camp, you will have lunch before resting and preparing for the summit attempt. Your guide will conduct a final equipment check and summit briefing, covering the expected conditions, pacing and safety procedures. An early dinner will be served before you rest for several hours in preparation for the midnight ascent.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Barafu to Uhuru Peak to Mweka Camp
paragraphs:
You will wake around midnight and begin the final ascent toward Uhuru Peak, the highest point of Mount Kilimanjaro and the highest point in Africa. The climb begins in darkness, with a slow and controlled ascent over volcanic scree toward the crater rim. Your guide will maintain a steady pace to help conserve energy and manage the effects of altitude. As dawn approaches, you will continue toward Uhuru Peak at 5,895 metres. UHURU PEAK – 5,895 M
After reaching the summit, you will have time to celebrate your achievement and take photographs before beginning the descent. You will descend toward Barafu Camp before continuing through the changing ecological zones toward Mweka Camp at approximately 3,100 metres. The descent is long, but the lower elevation provides welcome relief after the summit climb. Upon arriving at Mweka Camp, you will have dinner and a well-earned rest.

days.label: Day 08
days.title: Mweka Camp to Mweka Gate to Moshi/Arusha
paragraphs: After breakfast, you begin the final descent through the lush montane rainforest toward Mweka Gate. The trail gradually descends through the forest as the environment changes from high-altitude terrain to dense tropical vegetation. Upon reaching Mweka Gate, you will complete the park exit procedures and receive your Kilimanjaro summit certificate. You will then meet your vehicle for the transfer back to Moshi or Arusha, where you can check into your hotel, enjoy a hot shower and relax after completing your Mount Kilimanjaro trek.

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: The Lemosho Route is one of the most scenic approaches to Mount Kilimanjaro, beginning on the quiet western side of the mountain before crossing the spectacular Shira Plateau and joining the Southern Circuit. The route offers an excellent acclimatization profile, with gradual altitude gain and a key “climb high, sleep low” day at Lava Tower before descending into the Barranco Valley. As the trek progresses, the landscape changes from lush rainforest to open moorland, alpine desert and finally the Arctic Zone around the summit. The route also includes the famous Barranco Wall, a non-technical rock scramble, before continuing toward Barafu Camp for the summit attempt. After reaching Uhuru Peak at 5,895 metres, the descent follows the Mweka Route through the southern slopes of Kilimanjaro.

days.title: Moshi/Arusha to Shira Gate to Shira 1 Camp

The vehicle climbs through the forest and heath zones before reaching Shira Gate at approximately 3,500 metres, giving you a significant head start compared with routes that begin trekking from the lower rainforest. After completing the registration and park entry procedures, you begin a relatively short trek across the open Shira Plateau toward Shira 1 Camp at approximately 3,610 metres. The open landscape provides the first views of Kibo, the highest volcanic cone of Kilimanjaro, rising ahead of you. Upon arrival at camp, you will have time to rest, enjoy dinner and settle in for your first night at altitude.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Shira 1 to Shira 2 Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you continue across the beautiful Shira Plateau toward Shira 2 Camp. Today’s route is relatively gentle, providing valuable time for your body to adjust to the altitude before the trail becomes more demanding. The landscape is characterized by open moorland, volcanic formations and expansive views toward Kibo and the surrounding highlands. You will arrive at Shira 2 Camp at approximately 3,850 metres, where you will have time to rest and, if conditions permit, take a short acclimatization walk around the camp. Dinner will be served before an overnight rest.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Shira 2 to Barranco Camp
paragraphs: Today is an important acclimatization day as you follow the principle of “climb high, sleep low.” You leave Shira 2 and gradually ascend toward Lava Tower at approximately 4,600 metres. The landscape becomes increasingly barren as you enter the alpine desert zone. After spending time at Lava Tower, the trail descends into the beautiful Barranco Valley, allowing you to sleep at a lower elevation than the highest point reached during the day. The descent brings a dramatic change in scenery, with the towering Barranco Wall and Southern Icefields creating an impressive backdrop. You will arrive at Barranco Camp at approximately 3,960 metres, where you will have dinner and rest.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Barranco to Karanga Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you begin the ascent of the famous Barranco Wall. The climb involves scrambling over sections of rock and using your hands for balance in places. It is non-technical and does not require specialist climbing equipment, but it provides an exciting and physically engaging section of the trek. After reaching the top of the wall, the trail continues across a series of ridges and valleys toward Karanga Camp at approximately 4,035 metres. The day’s relatively short distance gives you time to rest and continue preparing your body for the summit ascent. After dinner, you will rest at camp.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Karanga to Barafu Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave Karanga Camp and continue toward Barafu Camp at approximately 4,673 metres, the main base camp for the summit attempt. The trail becomes increasingly barren as you move deeper into the alpine desert zone, with little vegetation surviving at this elevation. Although the distance is short, the altitude gain is significant. Upon reaching Barafu Camp, you will have time to rest and recover. Your guide will conduct a summit briefing and final equipment check, ensuring that you are properly prepared for the overnight ascent. An early dinner will be served before you rest for several hours in preparation for the summit climb.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Barafu to Uhuru Peak to Mweka Camp
paragraphs: You will wake around midnight and begin the final ascent toward Uhuru Peak, the highest point of Mount Kilimanjaro and the highest point in Africa. The climb begins in darkness, with your headlamp lighting the volcanic trail as you slowly ascend toward the crater rim. Your guide will maintain a steady and controlled pace to conserve energy and help manage the effects of altitude. As dawn approaches, you will reach the summit area and continue toward Uhuru Peak at 5,895 metres. UHURU PEAK – 5,895 M After reaching the summit, you will have time to celebrate your achievement and take photographs before beginning the descent. You will descend toward Barafu Camp before continuing down through the changing ecological zones toward Mweka Camp at approximately 3,100 metres. The descent is long, but the lower elevation and warmer conditions provide welcome relief after the summit climb. You will arrive at Mweka Camp for dinner and a well-earned rest.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Mweka Camp to Mweka Gate to Moshi/Arusha
paragraphs: After breakfast, you begin the final descent through the lush montane rainforest toward Mweka Gate. The trail gradually descends through the forest as the mountain environment changes from high-altitude terrain to a warm, dense tropical landscape. Upon reaching Mweka Gate, you will complete the park exit procedures and receive your Kilimanjaro summit certificate. You will then meet your vehicle for the transfer back to Moshi or Arusha, where you can check into your hotel, enjoy a hot shower and relax after completing your Mount Kilimanjaro trek.

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: The Shira Route is a scenic western approach to Mount Kilimanjaro that begins high on the mountain at the Shira Plateau. By driving directly to the high-altitude trailhead, the route skips the lower rainforest section and allows trekkers to begin their adventure in the open moorland of the plateau. The route follows the western side of Kilimanjaro before joining the Southern Circuit, where trekkers experience the dramatic Lava Tower, Barranco Valley and the famous Barranco Wall. It then continues toward Barafu Camp for the summit attempt before descending through the Mweka Route. The high starting elevation makes proper acclimatization particularly important. The itinerary therefore includes gradual altitude gain and a “climb high, sleep low” section through Lava Tower and Barranco.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Moshi/Arusha to Rongai Gate to Simba Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you will meet your guide and complete a final equipment and gear check before beginning the drive toward the northern side of Mount Kilimanjaro. The journey takes you around the mountain toward Rongai Gate, close to the Kenyan border. This quieter approach provides a noticeably different experience from the more frequently used southern routes. After completing registration and park entry formalities at the gate, the trek begins through cultivated farmland before gradually entering the pine forest. The trail climbs steadily toward Simba Camp at approximately 2,625 metres, where you will have dinner and settle in for your first night on the mountain.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Simba Camp to Second Cave
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave Simba Camp and continue climbing as the pine forest gradually gives way to open moorland. The trail provides increasingly wide views across the northern side of Kilimanjaro, with the dramatic spires of Mawenzi beginning to appear as you gain elevation. The steady ascent continues toward Second Cave Camp at approximately 3,450 metres. After arriving at camp, you will have time to rest, enjoy your meals and take in the surrounding mountain scenery.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Second Cave to Kikelelwa Camp
paragraphs: Today’s trek is shorter and follows a gradual ascent through open moorland. The trail continues toward the Mawenzi side of the mountain, with increasingly impressive views across the surrounding landscape. On clear days, the northern plains and parts of Kenya can be seen in the distance. You will continue to Kikelelwa Camp at approximately 3,600 metres, situated beneath the dramatic slopes of Mawenzi. The relatively gentle pace of the day provides valuable time for your body to adjust to the increasing altitude before the higher stages of the trek. Dinner will be served at camp before an overnight rest.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Kikelelwa to Mawenzi Tarn Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave Kikelelwa Camp and begin a steeper ascent toward Mawenzi Tarn. As you gain altitude, the vegetation becomes increasingly sparse and the landscape changes into the alpine desert zone. The trail leads toward one of the most spectacular camping locations on Kilimanjaro, Mawenzi Tarn Camp at approximately 4,330 metres. The camp sits beside a small alpine tarn and beneath the dramatic volcanic spires of Mawenzi. You will have time to rest and take in the remarkable surroundings while allowing your body additional time to adapt to the higher altitude. After dinner, you will rest at camp.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Mawenzi Tarn to Kibo Hut
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave Mawenzi Tarn and begin crossing the broad, exposed Saddle, the high-altitude desert between Mawenzi and Kibo. The landscape becomes increasingly barren as you approach the slopes of Kibo, the highest volcanic cone of Kilimanjaro. The trail continues across the Saddle toward Kibo Hut at approximately 4,700 metres, the final overnight stop before the summit. Upon arrival, you will have time to rest and prepare your summit equipment. Your guide will conduct a final summit briefing and equipment check. An early dinner will be served before you rest for several hours in preparation for the midnight summit ascent.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Kibo Hut to Uhuru Peak to Horombo Hut
paragraphs: You will wake around midnight and begin the final ascent toward Uhuru Peak, the highest point on Mount Kilimanjaro and the highest point in Africa. The climb begins in darkness, with a slow and steady ascent over volcanic scree toward the crater rim. Your guide will maintain a controlled pace to help conserve energy and manage the effects of altitude. As you approach the crater rim, the landscape becomes increasingly dramatic. You will continue toward Uhuru Peak at 5,895 metres, aiming to reach the summit around sunrise. UHURU PEAK – 5,895 M After reaching the summit, you will have time to celebrate your achievement and take photographs before beginning the descent. The route descends from Kibo and then joins the Marangu Route, providing a different perspective of the mountain from the northern approach used during the ascent. You will continue downward through the alpine and moorland zones toward Horombo Hut at approximately 3,720 metres. After arriving at Horombo, you will have dinner and a well-earned rest following the long summit day.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Horombo Hut to Marangu Gate to Moshi/Arusha
paragraphs: After breakfast, you begin the final descent from Horombo Hut toward Marangu Gate. The trail gradually passes from the open moorland back into the lush montane rainforest, bringing you through the same lower ecological zones that characterize the Marangu side of Kilimanjaro. As you descend, the air becomes warmer and the vegetation becomes denser, marking the final stage of your trek. Upon reaching Marangu Gate, you will complete the park exit procedures and receive your Kilimanjaro summit certificate. You will then meet your vehicle and transfer back to Moshi or Arusha, where you can check into your hotel, enjoy a hot shower and relax after completing your Mount Kilimanjaro trek.

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: The Rongai Route is the only Kilimanjaro route that approaches the mountain from the north, close to the Kenyan border. This side of the mountain is generally drier, quieter and less crowded than the southern approaches. The route provides a gradual ascent through a variety of landscapes, from cultivated farmland and pine forest to open moorland, alpine desert and the high-altitude Arctic Zone. It also passes beneath the dramatic peaks of Mawenzi, including the beautiful Mawenzi Tarn, before crossing the Saddle toward Kibo. After reaching the summit of Uhuru Peak at 5,895 metres, the descent follows the Marangu Route, allowing you to experience a different side of Kilimanjaro.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Moshi/Arusha to Marangu Gate to Mandara Hut
paragraphs: After breakfast, you will meet your guide for a final equipment and gear check before departing from your hotel in Moshi or Arusha. The drive to Marangu Gate at approximately 1,860 metres is relatively short. Upon arrival, your guide will complete the park registration and entry procedures while the trekking team prepares for the climb. The trail begins by entering the lush montane rainforest, where tall trees, dense vegetation and moss-covered surroundings create a cool and beautiful environment. Colobus monkeys and other forest wildlife may be seen along the trail. You will continue gradually uphill through the forest before reaching Mandara Hut at approximately 2,700 metres, the first overnight stop. After arriving at the hut, you will have time to settle in and rest. Weather and time permitting, you may take a short walk toward Maundi Crater for views across the surrounding landscape. Dinner will be served at the hut before an overnight rest.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Mandara Hut to Horombo Hut
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave Mandara Hut and continue climbing as the rainforest gradually gives way to open moorland and heath vegetation. The landscape becomes increasingly expansive, and you begin to experience the characteristic high-altitude scenery of Kilimanjaro. On clear days, you can see the distinctive peaks of Mawenzi and Kibo rising above the surrounding landscape. The trail continues steadily toward Horombo Hut at approximately 3,720 metres. Upon arrival, you will have time to rest, enjoy your meals and prepare for the following day’s acclimatization hike.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Acclimatization Day at Horombo Hut
paragraphs: Today is dedicated to acclimatization. After a relaxed breakfast, you will undertake an optional acclimatization hike toward Zebra Rocks at approximately 4,390 metres. The hike provides an opportunity to gain additional altitude during the day before returning to sleep at the lower elevation of Horombo Hut. Zebra Rocks are named for their distinctive black-and-white striped appearance and provide an interesting feature within the high-altitude landscape. After the hike, you will return to Horombo Hut for lunch and have the remainder of the day to rest, recover and prepare for the ascent toward Kibo. Dinner will be served at the hut before an early night’s rest.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Horombo Hut to Kibo Hut
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave Horombo Hut and begin the gradual ascent toward Kibo Hut. The trail crosses the famous Saddle, the broad and exposed high-altitude area lying between the volcanic cones of Mawenzi and Kibo. Vegetation becomes increasingly sparse, creating a stark, almost lunar landscape. The steady ascent continues across the alpine desert toward Kibo Hut at approximately 4,700 metres, the final overnight stop before the summit. Upon arrival, you will have time to rest and prepare your summit equipment. Your guide will conduct a final briefing covering the summit ascent, pacing, clothing, hydration and safety procedures. An early dinner will be served before you rest for several hours in preparation for the midnight summit departure.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Kibo Hut to Uhuru Peak to Horombo Hut
paragraphs: You will wake around midnight and begin the final ascent toward Uhuru Peak, the highest point on Mount Kilimanjaro and the highest elevation in Africa. The climb begins in darkness, with a slow and steady ascent over volcanic scree toward the crater rim. The pace is deliberately controlled to conserve energy and help manage the effects of altitude. You will continue toward the crater rim before proceeding to Uhuru Peak at 5,895 metres. Reaching the summit around sunrise provides spectacular views across the surrounding landscape as the first light appears over Tanzania. UHURU PEAK – 5,895 M After celebrating your achievement and taking photographs at the summit, you will begin the descent. The route follows the same trail back toward Kibo Hut, where you will have a short rest before continuing down toward Horombo Hut. The descent provides welcome relief from the high-altitude environment as you return through the alpine and moorland zones. You will arrive at Horombo Hut at approximately 3,720 metres, where dinner and a well-earned night’s rest await.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Horombo Hut to Marangu Gate to Moshi/Arusha
paragraphs: After breakfast, you begin the final descent from Horombo Hut toward Marangu Gate. The trail takes you back through the moorland before gradually returning to the lush montane rainforest encountered on the first day. The changing vegetation provides a fitting conclusion to the trek. Upon reaching Marangu Gate, you will complete the park exit procedures and receive your Kilimanjaro summit certificate. You will then meet your vehicle for the transfer back to Moshi or Arusha, where you can check into your hotel, enjoy a hot shower and relax after completing your Mount Kilimanjaro trek.

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: The Marangu Route, popularly known as the “Coca-Cola Route,” is the only Kilimanjaro route offering overnight accommodation in permanent mountain huts rather than tents. Its gradual, well-established trail and additional acclimatization day make it one of the more approachable routes for trekkers who prefer hut accommodation. The route takes you through Kilimanjaro’s diverse ecological zones, beginning in the lush rainforest before continuing through moorland, alpine desert and the high arctic zone around the summit. The itinerary includes an acclimatization day at Horombo Hut, with an optional hike toward Zebra Rocks, allowing trekkers additional time to adjust to the altitude before continuing toward Kibo and the summit.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Moshi/Arusha to Marangu Gate to Mandara Hut
paragraphs: After breakfast at your hotel in Moshi or Arusha, you will meet your mountain crew and have a final check of your trekking equipment before driving to Marangu Gate, located at approximately 1,860 metres. At the gate, your guide will complete the registration and entry formalities while the porters prepare the equipment. Once everything is ready, the trek begins. The trail enters the beautiful montane rainforest, where the path is surrounded by tall trees, dense vegetation and moss-covered forest. You may also encounter monkeys and a variety of birdlife along the way. The trek continues gradually through the forest before reaching Mandara Hut at approximately 2,700 metres, your first overnight stop. Weather and time permitting, there may be an opportunity for a short walk to Maundi Crater before returning to the hut. After dinner, you will rest early in preparation for the following day’s trek.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Mandara Hut to Horombo Hut
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave Mandara Hut and continue climbing gradually as the dense rainforest gives way to open moorland and heath vegetation. As you gain elevation, the landscape becomes more open, with impressive views of Kibo and Mawenzi, the two major volcanic cones of Kilimanjaro. The trail continues steadily toward Horombo Hut. Since this is the express itinerary and there is no additional acclimatization day at Horombo, your guide will maintain a controlled pace, allowing you to conserve energy for the summit attempt. You arrive at Horombo Hut at approximately 3,720 metres, where you will have time to eat, rest and prepare for the following day’s ascent. Dinner will be served in the evening, followed by an early rest.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Horombo Hut to Kibo Hut
paragraphs: Today you leave Horombo and cross the high-altitude Saddle, the broad desert-like area separating Mawenzi and Kibo. Vegetation becomes increasingly sparse as you enter the alpine desert zone. The trail is exposed and the effects of altitude become more noticeable, so maintaining a slow and steady pace is important. The route continues across the Saddle toward Kibo Hut at approximately 4,700 metres, the final overnight stop before the summit. Upon arrival, you will have an early dinner and prepare your summit equipment. Your guide will brief you on the summit attempt, including pacing, clothing, hydration and safety procedures. You will then rest for several hours before beginning the summit climb around midnight. Early dinner: Approximately 17:00. Rest: Evening until midnight. Summit departure: Approximately 00:00

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Kibo Hut to Uhuru Peak to Marangu Gate
paragraphs: After reaching the summit, you will have a short period to celebrate, take photographs and enjoy the achievement before beginning the descent. The descent takes you back to Kibo Hut, where you will have a short rest and collect your remaining belongings before continuing down toward Horombo and eventually Marangu Gate. The descent through the moorland and rainforest provides a dramatic change from the barren summit landscape encountered earlier in the day. After reaching Marangu Gate, you will complete the exit formalities and receive your summit certificate before transferring back to your hotel in Moshi or Arusha.

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: The 4-day Marangu Express is the fastest hut-based itinerary to the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro. Known as the “Coca-Cola Route,” Marangu is the only Kilimanjaro route offering overnight accommodation in permanent mountain huts rather than tents. This itinerary is designed for trekkers with limited time, strong fitness and preferably previous high-altitude trekking experience. Unlike the longer 5- or 6-day Marangu itineraries, there is no additional acclimatization day at Horombo Hut. This makes the trek significantly more demanding, particularly because the summit attempt and descent are completed in one very long day. The route takes you through Kilimanjaro’s changing vegetation zones, from lush montane rainforest to open moorland, alpine desert and finally the arctic summit zone. The ultimate goal is Uhuru Peak at 5,895 metres, the highest point in Africa.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Moshi/Arusha to Umbwe Gate to Umbwe Cave Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast at your hotel, you will meet your guide and complete a thorough equipment check before departing for Umbwe Gate at approximately 1,600 metres. After registration and preparation at the gate, the trek begins with a steep and direct climb through dense montane rainforest. The Umbwe trail is known for its steep character from the very beginning, with the path following ridges and narrow sections through the forest. The demanding ascent requires a steady pace and careful footing. You will continue climbing through the forest toward Umbwe Cave Camp at approximately 2,850 metres. After arriving at camp, you will have dinner and rest in preparation for another demanding day.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Umbwe Cave to Barranco Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you continue the steep ascent as the dense forest gradually gives way to moorland vegetation. The trail becomes more exposed, revealing dramatic views of the surrounding mountain landscape and the Southern Icefields. You continue climbing toward the Barranco Valley, where the route joins the Southern Circuit. The day’s trek is relatively short in distance but remains demanding because of the steep terrain and increasing altitude. You arrive at Barranco Camp at approximately 3,960 metres, situated beneath the impressive Barranco Wall. After dinner, you will rest and prepare for the following day’s trek.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Barranco Camp to Karanga Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you begin the day with the ascent of the famous Barranco Wall. The climb involves scrambling over rock sections and using your hands for balance in places, but it is non-technical and does not require climbing equipment. Once above the wall, the trail continues across a series of ridges and valleys toward Karanga Camp at approximately 4,035 metres. This shorter day allows your body to continue adjusting to the increasing altitude while giving you time to rest before the ascent toward Barafu Camp. You will have dinner and spend the night at Karanga Camp.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Karanga to Barafu Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave Karanga Camp and continue toward Barafu Camp at approximately 4,673 metres. The landscape becomes increasingly barren as you enter the alpine desert zone, with little vegetation surviving at this elevation. The route is relatively short but involves a significant gain in altitude. Upon reaching Barafu Camp, you will have lunch and settle in for the afternoon. Your guide will conduct a detailed summit briefing and equipment check, ensuring that you have everything required for the summit attempt. An early dinner will be served before you rest for several hours in preparation for the midnight ascent to Uhuru Peak.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Barafu to Uhuru Peak to Mweka Camp
paragraphs: You will wake around midnight and begin the final ascent toward Uhuru Peak, the highest point in Africa. The climb begins slowly through the darkness as you ascend over volcanic scree toward the crater rim. Your guide will maintain a steady pace to help conserve energy and manage the effects of altitude. You will reach the summit around sunrise, where you can enjoy spectacular views across the surrounding landscape. UHURU PEAK – 5,895 M After reaching Uhuru Peak, you will spend a short time at the summit for photographs and celebration before beginning the descent. The descent takes you back toward Barafu Camp, where you will have a short rest before continuing toward Mweka Camp. As you descend, the landscape changes dramatically from the high alpine environment through moorland and eventually back into the rainforest. You will arrive at Mweka Camp at approximately 3,100 metres, where you will have dinner and rest after this long and demanding summit day.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Mweka Camp to Mweka Gate to Moshi/Arusha
paragraphs: After breakfast, you begin the final descent through the lush montane rainforest toward Mweka Gate. The trail gradually descends through the forest, providing a final opportunity to enjoy the vegetation and scenery of Kilimanjaro. Upon reaching Mweka Gate, you will complete the park exit procedures and receive your Kilimanjaro summit certificate. You will then meet your vehicle for the transfer back to your hotel in Moshi or Arusha, marking the end of your Mount Kilimanjaro trek.

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: The Umbwe Route is one of the steepest and most direct approaches to the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro. It begins with a demanding ascent through dense rainforest before joining the Southern Circuit at Barranco. The route is known for its dramatic scenery, quieter lower sections and challenging terrain. As the trek progresses, the landscape changes from rainforest to moorland, alpine desert and finally the arctic summit zone. The route is best suited to experienced and physically fit trekkers who are comfortable with steep ascents and challenging mountain terrain.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Arusha to Momella Gate to Miriakamba Hut
paragraphs: After breakfast, you will meet your guide for a final equipment check before departing from your hotel in Arusha. A short drive takes you to Momella Gate, where you will complete the park registration and entry formalities. An armed ranger will join the group in accordance with Arusha National Park regulations. The trek begins through the lower forest, where the trail passes through an area rich in wildlife. Buffalo, giraffe and colobus monkeys are among the animals that may be encountered along the route. You will continue climbing gradually through the forest toward Miriakamba Hut at approximately 2,514 metres. Upon arrival, you will have time to settle in, rest and enjoy dinner before an overnight stay at the hut.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Miriakamba Hut to Saddle Hut
paragraphs: After breakfast, you leave Miriakamba Hut and begin the ascent toward Saddle Hut. The trail gradually leaves the forest behind as the vegetation changes into open moorland. As you gain elevation, the views become more expansive, with the surrounding landscapes and, on clear days, Mount Kilimanjaro visible in the distance. You will arrive at Saddle Hut at approximately 3,570 metres, where you will have lunch and time to rest. If conditions permit, an optional acclimatization hike can be made to Little Meru at approximately 3,820 metres before returning to Saddle Hut. After dinner, you will rest early in preparation for the summit attempt.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Saddle Hut to Socialist Peak to Miriakamba Hut
paragraphs: You will wake around midnight and begin the summit ascent while the mountain is still quiet and dark. The trail climbs steadily toward Socialist Peak at 4,566 metres, with sections becoming increasingly steep as you approach the summit. The pace will be slow and controlled to help manage the altitude and conserve energy. You aim to reach the summit around sunrise. From Socialist Peak, you can enjoy panoramic views across northern Tanzania, with Mount Kilimanjaro visible on clear mornings. After spending some time at the summit, you begin the descent toward Saddle Hut before continuing through the moorland and forest to Miriakamba Hut. This is the longest and most physically demanding day of the trek.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Miriakamba Hut to Momella Gate to Arusha
paragraphs: After breakfast, you begin the final descent from Miriakamba Hut toward Momella Gate. The trail passes once again through the montane forest, providing another opportunity to observe wildlife along the lower slopes. Upon reaching Momella Gate, you will complete the park exit procedures and receive your Mount Meru trekking certificate. You will then meet your vehicle and transfer back to Arusha, where you will check into your hotel and have time to rest and recover after completing the trek.

extraSections.title: Route overview
paragraphs: Mount Meru is Tanzania’s second-highest mountain and an excellent acclimatization trek before attempting Mount Kilimanjaro. Standing at 4,566 metres, the trek provides valuable experience with high-altitude hiking while taking you through some of the most diverse landscapes of Arusha National Park. The lower slopes are rich in wildlife, with opportunities to encounter buffalo, giraffe and colobus monkeys as you trek through the forest. As you climb higher, the landscape changes from montane forest to open moorland and alpine terrain. The summit of Socialist Peak at 4,566 metres offers spectacular views across northern Tanzania, including impressive views of Mount Kilimanjaro on clear days. An armed ranger accompanies the expeditioners along the route as required within Arusha National Park because of the presence of wildlife on the lower sections of the mountain.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Arrival Arusha
paragraphs: Your Tanzania safari begins with your arrival at Kilimanjaro International Airport, where you will be met and transferred to your accommodation in Arusha. After checking in, you will receive a safari briefing and have time to relax and prepare for the days ahead. The evening is spent at leisure at the lodge, with dinner and overnight in Arusha.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Arusha to Tarangire
paragraphs: After breakfast, depart Arusha and travel towards Tarangire National Park. Upon arrival, begin your first full game-viewing experience in Tanzania. Tarangire is known for its large elephant herds and distinctive baobab trees, which create a dramatic backdrop across the park. Enjoy a picnic lunch during the day’s game drive before continuing to explore the park through the afternoon. Later, proceed to your accommodation for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Tarangire to Lake Manyara
paragraphs: After breakfast, enjoy a morning game drive in Tarangire before departing for Lake Manyara National Park. Continue towards Lake Manyara and, after arrival, begin an afternoon game drive through the park. Explore the varied landscape around the lake, looking for tree-climbing lions, flamingos, hippos and other wildlife. The park also provides opportunities for bird watching and photography. Return to your accommodation in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Lake Manyara to Serengeti
paragraphs: After breakfast, depart Lake Manyara and travel towards the Serengeti. The journey takes you through the Ngorongoro area, with an opportunity to visit Olduvai Gorge along the way. Continue through the changing landscapes as you make your way towards the Serengeti. Wildlife viewing begins along the route, with further game viewing as you enter the Serengeti ecosystem. Continue to your accommodation for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Full Day Serengeti
paragraphs: Today is dedicated to exploring the Serengeti. Set out for morning game viewing across the vast plains before continuing with an afternoon game drive. Depending on the season and location, you may encounter wildlife associated with the migration, as well as the Serengeti’s famous big cats. Enjoy a picnic lunch during the day’s exploration before continuing deeper into the park. Return to your accommodation in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Serengeti Exploration
paragraphs: Continue your exploration of the Serengeti with another full day of game viewing. The day’s route may focus around the Seronera area or extend towards the Western Corridor, depending on the safari programme. Spend the day exploring the park’s landscapes and searching for wildlife while allowing plenty of time for photography and observation. Return to your accommodation in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Serengeti Game Drives
paragraphs: Enjoy another full day in the Serengeti, exploring the plains and different wildlife areas. The day is designed around extensive game viewing, giving you further opportunities to encounter the animals that make the Serengeti one of Tanzania’s best-known wildlife destinations. A full-day game drive with packed lunch allows you to spend more time inside the park. For those interested, an optional hot-air balloon safari can be arranged. Return to the lodge in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 08
days.title: Serengeti to Ngorongoro
paragraphs: After breakfast, begin your journey from the Serengeti towards the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Enjoy wildlife viewing along the route as you leave the Serengeti behind and travel towards the Ngorongoro highlands. Arrive at the crater rim in the afternoon, where you can enjoy views across the spectacular landscape before settling into your accommodation. Dinner and overnight at the lodge.

days.label: Day 09
days.title: Ngorongoro Crater Tour
paragraphs: After breakfast, descend approximately 600 metres into the Ngorongoro Crater for a full day of wildlife exploration. The crater floor provides a remarkable setting for game viewing, with opportunities to encounter a wide range of wildlife, including the Big Five and, with luck, rhino. Enjoy a picnic lunch around the hippo pool before continuing with further game viewing across the crater floor. In the afternoon, begin the ascent from the crater and return to the lodge for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 10
days.title: Ngorongoro to Arusha
paragraphs: Enjoy your final morning in the Ngorongoro area before beginning the journey back to Arusha. For guests interested in a cultural experience, an optional Maasai village visit can be arranged before continuing the journey. Proceed to Arusha and transfer to the airport for your onward flight, marking the end of your Tanzania safari.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Arrival Arusha
paragraphs: Upon arrival at Kilimanjaro International Airport, you will be met and transferred to your accommodation in Arusha. After checking in, you will have time to settle in and relax. A safari briefing will be provided, giving you an overview of the journey ahead and helping you prepare for your first day in the national parks. Enjoy dinner and overnight at the lodge.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Arusha to Tarangire
paragraphs: After breakfast, depart Arusha and travel towards Tarangire National Park. Upon arrival, begin your first game drive through the park. Tarangire is known for its large elephant herds and distinctive baobab trees, creating a memorable landscape for wildlife viewing and photography. Spend the day exploring different areas of the park, with opportunities to encounter a variety of wildlife. Continue to your accommodation in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Tarangire to Serengeti
paragraphs: After breakfast, depart Tarangire and travel towards the Serengeti through the Ngorongoro area. Along the way, stop at Olduvai Gorge before continuing towards the Serengeti. The changing landscapes provide opportunities for wildlife viewing as you make your way towards the park. Arrive in the Serengeti for an afternoon game drive before proceeding to your accommodation. Enjoy dinner and overnight in the Serengeti.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Full Day Serengeti
paragraphs: Spend a full day exploring the Serengeti. Begin with a morning game drive across the plains, searching for the park’s abundant wildlife and the Big Five. Continue with further game viewing in the afternoon, exploring different areas of the Serengeti. The open landscapes provide excellent opportunities for wildlife photography and observing animals in their natural surroundings. Return to your accommodation in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Serengeti Game Viewing
paragraphs: Continue your Serengeti experience with another full day of game viewing. Explore the plains and different wildlife areas, allowing plenty of time to search for predators, elephants and other wildlife. An optional hot-air balloon safari can be arranged for guests who would like to experience the Serengeti from above. Continue with game viewing throughout the day before returning to your lodge for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Serengeti to Ngorongoro
paragraphs: After breakfast, begin your journey from the Serengeti towards the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Enjoy a morning game drive as you leave the Serengeti before continuing towards the Ngorongoro highlands. Arrive at the crater rim in the afternoon and take in the views across the spectacular crater landscape. Settle into your accommodation and enjoy dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Ngorongoro Crater
paragraphs: After breakfast, descend into the Ngorongoro Crater for a full day of wildlife viewing. The crater floor provides opportunities to encounter a wide variety of wildlife, including the Big Five. Explore the different areas of the crater while taking in its dramatic scenery. Enjoy a picnic lunch before continuing with further game viewing. In the afternoon, ascend from the crater and return to your lodge for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 08
days.title: Ngorongoro to Arusha
paragraphs: After breakfast, begin your journey back to Arusha. An optional cultural visit can be arranged for guests who would like to experience a Maasai village before continuing to Arusha. Upon arrival in Arusha, you will be transferred to the airport for your onward journey. This marks the end of your Tanzania safari.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Arrival Arusha
paragraphs: Your luxury Tanzania safari begins with a VIP airport transfer from Kilimanjaro International Airport to your luxury accommodation in Arusha. Upon arrival, settle into the hotel and enjoy a welcome briefing covering the safari ahead. The remainder of the day is at leisure, giving you time to relax and prepare for your journey through Tanzania’s northern safari circuit. Enjoy dinner and overnight in Arusha.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Arusha to Tarangire
paragraphs: After breakfast, depart Arusha by private transfer towards Tarangire National Park. Upon arrival, begin your first game drive through the park. Tarangire is known for its large elephant herds and impressive baobab trees, creating a distinctive landscape for wildlife viewing. Continue with game viewing through the park before proceeding to your luxury accommodation. Enjoy the evening surrounded by the atmosphere of the Tarangire wilderness, followed by dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Tarangire Exploration
paragraphs: Spend a full day exploring Tarangire National Park. Begin with wildlife viewing across the park before experiencing a walking safari, allowing you to experience the landscape from a different perspective. Later, continue with further game viewing before an evening night drive, offering another way to experience the wilderness. The day concludes with a bush dinner before returning to your accommodation for overnight.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Tarangire to Lake Manyara
paragraphs: After breakfast, depart Tarangire and travel towards Lake Manyara National Park. Upon arrival, explore the park and its varied landscapes. One of the day’s highlights is a canopy walk, offering a different perspective of the surrounding environment. Continue with wildlife viewing, keeping watch for the tree-climbing lions and other wildlife found in the park. Proceed to your luxury accommodation for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Lake Manyara to Serengeti
paragraphs: After breakfast, depart Lake Manyara and travel towards the Serengeti. Enjoy the scenic journey through the northern Tanzania landscape, with a stop at Olduvai Gorge along the way. Continue into the Serengeti and begin exploring the park as you enter the ecosystem. Wildlife viewing continues before proceeding to your luxury accommodation. Enjoy dinner and overnight in the Serengeti.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Serengeti - Central
paragraphs: Spend the day exploring the central Serengeti around the Seronera area. The region provides opportunities to search for the Serengeti’s famous big cats and other wildlife. Continue exploring the surrounding plains and wildlife areas, with the possibility of encountering seasonal river crossings depending on the timing and location of the migration. Return to your luxury accommodation in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Serengeti Balloon Safari
paragraphs: Begin the morning with an optional hot-air balloon safari over the Serengeti at dawn. After the flight, enjoy a champagne breakfast before returning to the day’s safari programme. Spend the afternoon exploring the Serengeti on a game drive, searching for wildlife across the plains and taking in the changing scenery. Return to your accommodation for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 08
days.title: Serengeti - Western Corridor
paragraphs: After breakfast, continue towards the Western Serengeti and explore the area around the Grumeti River. The western region offers a different landscape and wildlife experience from central Serengeti. Continue with game viewing before arriving at your luxury mobile camp. Enjoy dinner and overnight in the Western Serengeti.

days.label: Day 09
days.title: Western Serengeti
paragraphs: Spend a full day exploring the Western Serengeti. Continue searching for wildlife across the region, with particular attention to migration herds and areas around the river where wildlife activity can be experienced. Enjoy a full day of premium game viewing and photography before returning to your accommodation in the evening. Dinner and overnight at the camp.

days.label: Day 10
days.title: Serengeti to Ngorongoro
paragraphs: After breakfast, enjoy a morning game drive as you begin your journey from the Serengeti towards the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Travel towards the crater highlands, taking in the changing scenery as the landscape transitions from the Serengeti plains towards the Ngorongoro area. Arrive at your luxury accommodation on the crater rim and enjoy the spectacular surroundings. Dinner and overnight at the lodge.

days.label: Day 11
days.title: Ngorongoro Crater
paragraphs: After breakfast, descend into the Ngorongoro Crater for a private full-day wildlife experience. Explore the crater floor in search of the Big Five and other wildlife while enjoying the unique scenery of the crater. A gourmet picnic lunch will be served during the crater tour before you continue with further wildlife viewing. In the evening, ascend from the crater and return to your luxury lodge.

days.label: Day 12
days.title: Ngorongoro to Arusha
paragraphs: Enjoy a relaxed morning at your accommodation before beginning your journey back towards Arusha. A cultural visit can be arranged during the journey for guests interested in experiencing a Maasai community. Continue to Arusha for your VIP departure transfer and onward flight arrangements. This marks the end of your luxury Tanzania safari.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Dar es Salaam to Selous
paragraphs: Your safari begins with a morning flight from Dar es Salaam to Selous. Upon arrival, transfer to your camp and settle in before heading out for your first experience of the Selous wilderness. In the afternoon, enjoy a boat safari along the Rufiji River. The river provides opportunities to see hippos, crocodiles and a variety of birdlife while experiencing the landscape from the water. Return to camp in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Walking Safari & Boat Safari
paragraphs: Begin the morning with a walking safari, experiencing the wilderness on foot and exploring the surrounding landscape. After returning to camp, enjoy lunch and some time to relax before heading out for an afternoon game drive. Later in the evening, enjoy another boat cruise along the Rufiji River, providing further opportunities to observe hippos, crocodiles and birdlife. Return to camp for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Selous Exploration
paragraphs: Today is dedicated to exploring Selous on a full-day game drive. Travel through different areas of the reserve, exploring its varied landscapes and searching for wildlife. The day’s viewing may include lions, elephants, wild dogs and other species. Enjoy a bush lunch during the day’s exploration before continuing with further game viewing. Return to camp in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Selous to Ruaha
paragraphs: After breakfast, transfer for your flight from Selous to Ruaha. Upon arrival, continue to your accommodation and settle in before heading out for an afternoon game drive. Explore the Ruaha landscape and areas around the Great Ruaha River, searching for wildlife as you begin your experience in Tanzania’s southern wilderness. Return to camp in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Ruaha Game Drives
paragraphs: Spend a full day exploring Ruaha National Park. Enjoy morning and afternoon game drives through the park, exploring its varied landscapes and searching for some of the wildlife that makes Ruaha distinctive. The day provides opportunities to encounter wild dogs, elephants and other wildlife while enjoying the park’s remote setting. Return to your accommodation in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Ruaha Walking Safari
paragraphs: Start the day with an early morning walking safari accompanied by an armed ranger. Explore the wilderness on foot before returning to camp for breakfast and time to relax. In the afternoon, head out for another game drive through Ruaha. Later, spend time around the river area, taking in the landscape and wildlife activity. Return to camp for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Ruaha Exploration
paragraphs: Continue exploring Ruaha with a full day of game viewing. Travel through different habitats, taking in the park’s distinctive landscapes and baobab trees while searching for predators and other wildlife. Enjoy lunch at the lodge or as a picnic during the day’s activities before continuing with further game viewing. Return to camp in the evening for dinner and overnight.

days.label: Day 08
days.title: Fly Camping Experience
paragraphs: Today offers the opportunity to experience Ruaha in a more adventurous way. For guests choosing the optional fly-camping experience, head into the wilderness for a walking safari followed by an evening bush dinner beneath the stars. Alternatively, guests may remain at the standard camp and enjoy the regular safari programme. Spend the night either under the stars as part of the fly-camping experience or at the standard accommodation.

days.label: Day 09
days.title: Full Day Ruaha
paragraphs: Enjoy your final full day exploring Ruaha National Park. Take part in morning and afternoon game drives, visiting different areas of the park and continuing the search for wildlife. This is an opportunity to enjoy further photography and take in the remote wilderness before your departure the following day. Return to camp for your final dinner and overnight in Ruaha.

days.label: Day 10
days.title: Ruaha to Dar es Salaam & Departure
paragraphs: Begin the final morning with a game drive, providing one last opportunity to experience Ruaha and encounter wildlife. After the morning activities, transfer for your flight back to Dar es Salaam. Upon arrival, continue with your city transfer or onward flight arrangements. This marks the end of your southern Tanzania safari.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Nairobi – Ol Pejeta Conservancy – Afternoon Game Drive
paragraphs: Depart Nairobi in the morning and drive towards Nanyuki, enjoying the scenic countryside and views of Mount Kenya along the way.
Upon arrival at Ol Pejeta Conservancy, proceed to the lodge or tented camp for check-in and lunch.

In the afternoon, head out for your first game drive across the conservancy’s beautiful landscapes. Explore the open grasslands and riverine areas in search of elephants, lions, buffaloes, giraffes, zebras, rhinos and other wildlife.
Ol Pejeta is particularly renowned for its successful rhino conservation programme and is home to an impressive diversity of wildlife.
Return to your accommodation in the evening for dinner and overnight.
Overnight: Lodge or tented camp in Ol Pejeta.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Full-Day Game Drive – Chimpanzee Sanctuary – Rhino Conservation Experience
paragraphs: After an early breakfast, depart for a morning game drive across the conservancy. Explore different wildlife habitats while looking out for predators, elephants, rhinos, zebras and other wildlife.

Later, visit the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary, Kenya’s only chimpanzee sanctuary. Learn about the rescued chimpanzees, their stories and the conservation work dedicated to their care and protection.
Proceed to the Morani Information Centre, where you can learn more about Ol Pejeta’s wildlife conservation initiatives and visit Baraka, the blind black rhino.

You may also arrange a special visit to see the northern white rhinos, one of the conservancy’s most remarkable conservation stories. This experience requires advance booking and an additional activity fee.
Enjoy lunch before continuing with an afternoon game drive, exploring more of the conservancy and its diverse wildlife.
Return to your accommodation for dinner and overnight.
Overnight: Lodge or tented camp in Ol Pejeta.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Morning Game Drive – Ol Pejeta – Nairobi
paragraphs: Wake up early for a morning game drive, one of the best times to explore the conservancy as many animals are active during the cooler hours.
Enjoy the opportunity to spot wildlife across the open plains while taking in the beautiful morning scenery.
Return to the lodge for breakfast and some time to relax before checking out.
Begin your journey back to Nairobi, arriving in the afternoon.
This marks the end of your Ol Pejeta Conservancy safari with Mohakin Climbers.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Nanyuki – Aberdare Ranges – Mount Satima – Table Mountain
paragraphs: Depart Nanyuki early in the morning and drive towards the northern Aberdare ranges. Upon arrival at the designated trailhead, meet your mountain guide and complete the necessary park entry arrangements before beginning the hike.
Start trekking through the beautiful open moorlands, gradually ascending towards Mount Satima, the highest peak in the Aberdare Ranges at approximately 4,001 m.
Along the way, encounter impressive rock formations, unique alpine vegetation and the spectacular Dragon’s Teeth, one of the most distinctive natural features of the Aberdares.
Upon reaching Mount Satima, enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding mountain ranges before continuing towards Table Mountain.
Explore the scenic high-altitude landscape before proceeding to the designated camping area. Settle into camp, enjoy dinner and spend the night surrounded by the beautiful Aberdare wilderness.

Highest elevation: 4,001 m
Hiking time: Full-day hike
Habitat: Moorland and alpine vegetation
Overnight: Designated campsite

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Table Mountain – Aberdare Ranges – Nanyuki
paragraphs: Wake up to the beautiful mountain scenery and enjoy breakfast at camp.
After breakfast, continue exploring the Table Mountain area, taking in the surrounding valleys, ridges and unique high-altitude vegetation.
Begin the descent towards the designated exit point, enjoying the final views of the Aberdare landscape along the way.
Upon reaching the trailhead, meet your vehicle for the return journey to Nanyuki.
This marks the end of your Mount Satima and Table Mountain expedition with Mohakin Climbers.

Hiking time: Depending on the selected descent route
Habitat: Alpine moorland and mountain vegetation

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Nanyuki – Mutubio Gate – Elephant Hill Summit – Nanyuki
paragraphs: Depart Nanyuki early in the morning and drive towards Mutubio Gate in the Aberdare National Park.
Upon arrival, complete the park entry procedures and meet your mountain guide before beginning the hike.

Start trekking through the dense bamboo forest, gradually ascending along the Elephant Hill trail. As you gain elevation, the forest gives way to open moorland, featuring giant heather, unique alpine vegetation and spectacular mountain scenery.
Continue climbing towards the famous Dragon’s Teeth and the distinctive moorland ridges before proceeding to the summit of Elephant Hill.

Upon reaching the summit, take time to enjoy the breathtaking views of the Aberdare ranges, surrounding valleys and the beautiful landscapes below. Enjoy your packed lunch and capture memorable photographs before beginning the descent.
Follow the same trail back towards Mutubio Gate. Upon arrival, complete the park exit procedures and meet your vehicle for the return journey to Nanyuki.
This marks the end of your Elephant Hill hiking adventure with Mohakin Climbers.

Hiking details:
Starting elevation: Approximately 2,500 m
Highest elevation: Approximately 3,658 m
Hiking distance: Approximately 10–14 km return
Hiking time: Approximately 6–8 hours
Habitat: Bamboo forest, moorland and alpine vegetation

whatToCarry: Warm clothing and a waterproof jacket

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Into the Forest – Canopy Walkway – Blue Pools – Nanyuki
paragraphs: Your adventure begins with an early departure from Nanyuki as you head towards the beautiful Ngare Ndare Forest, a hidden natural treasure at the foothills of Mount Kenya.

On arrival, meet your local ranger and begin exploring this ancient indigenous forest. Follow scenic forest trails surrounded by towering trees, fresh mountain air and the sounds of nature. Keep an eye out for wildlife, colourful birds and the forest’s fascinating plant life.

The adventure continues with a walk across the famous canopy walkway, suspended high above the forest floor. Take in the breathtaking views from above the treetops and enjoy a unique perspective of the forest.

Continue deeper into the forest to discover its beautiful waterfalls and remarkable blue pools. These crystal-clear natural pools offer a perfect spot to relax, take photographs and, where conditions permit, enjoy a refreshing swim.

After exploring the forest and enjoying time by the pools, take a break for lunch before making your way back along the forest trails. Meet your vehicle and return to Nanyuki with wonderful memories of a day spent discovering one of Kenya’s most beautiful natural destinations.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Nanyuki – Chogoria – Mount Kenya Bandas
paragraphs: Depart from Nanyuki and travel to Chogoria, where you meet the mountain crew and prepare for the expedition. Continue by vehicle through the forest to the designated roadhead. Begin trekking through the bamboo and indigenous forest towards Mount Kenya Bandas, enjoying the beautiful forest scenery along the way.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Mount Kenya Bandas – Lake Ellis
paragraphs: Continue ascending through the forest and open moorland towards Lake Ellis. Enjoy impressive views of the surrounding valleys and mountain peaks as the landscape changes with altitude. Arrive at Lake Ellis and settle into camp.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Lake Ellis – Mintos Camp
paragraphs: Proceed towards Mintos Camp through the spectacular alpine landscape. The route offers beautiful views of the Gorges Valley and Mount Kenya’s rugged terrain. Arrive at camp, rest and prepare for the summit attempt.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Mintos Camp – Point Lenana – Austrian Hut
paragraphs: Begin the summit ascent before dawn towards Point Lenana (4,985 m). Reach the summit in time to enjoy the sunrise over the surrounding mountain landscape. After celebrating your achievement, descend towards Austrian Hut (4,790 m), the base for the Nelion technical climb.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Austrian Hut – Nelion Peak – Howell Bivouac
paragraphs: Begin the technical ascent of Nelion (5,188 m) via the Normal Route. Cross the Lewis Glacier approach before tackling the multi-pitch rock climbing sections under the supervision of an experienced technical climbing guide.

Navigate the exposed rock faces and climbing pitches towards the summit of Nelion, the second-highest peak of Mount Kenya. After reaching the summit, continue to Howell Bivouac for an overnight stay, subject to weather and climbing conditions.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Howell Bivouac – Austrian Hut – Shipton’s Camp
paragraphs: Descend from Nelion using established abseil points under the guidance of your climbing team. Return to Austrian Hut and continue towards Shipton’s Camp via a guide-approved route on the upper mountain. This is a demanding descent following the technical climb.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Shipton’s Camp – Old Moses Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, descend through the scenic Mackinder Valley, passing through the alpine moorland towards Old Moses Camp. Enjoy the changing landscapes as you gradually descend to a lower altitude.

days.label: Day 08
days.title: Old Moses Camp – Sirimon Gate – Nanyuki
paragraphs: Complete the final descent to Sirimon Gate, where your vehicle will be waiting. Meet your transfer team and return to Nanyuki, marking the end of your Mount Kenya Nelion technical climbing expedition.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Mount Kenya Bandas – Lake Ellis
paragraphs: Continue ascending through the forest and open moorland towards Lake Ellis. Enjoy impressive views of the surrounding valleys and mountain peaks as the landscape changes with altitude. Arrive at Lake Ellis and settle into camp.

days.label: Day 03
days.title: Lake Ellis – Mintos Camp
paragraphs: Proceed towards Mintos Camp through the spectacular alpine landscape. The route offers beautiful views of the Gorges Valley and Mount Kenya’s rugged terrain. Arrive at camp, rest and prepare for the summit stages ahead.

days.label: Day 04
days.title: Mintos Camp – Point Lenana – Shipton’s Camp
paragraphs: Begin the summit ascent before dawn towards Point Lenana (4,985 m). Reach the summit in time to enjoy the sunrise over Mount Kenya’s dramatic peaks and surrounding landscapes.
After celebrating your achievement, descend towards Shipton’s Camp on the Sirimon side. This is the main base camp for the technical ascent of Batian via the North Face.

days.label: Day 05
days.title: Shipton’s Camp – Batian Peak – Shipton’s Camp
paragraphs: Begin the technical climbing expedition with an early start towards Batian (5,199 m), the highest peak of Mount Kenya.

Follow the North Face Standard Route, tackling exposed rock faces, chimneys, ledges and challenging multi-pitch climbing sections. The ascent requires advanced climbing skills, proper rope management and the guidance of an experienced technical climbing team.

Reach the summit of Batian and enjoy the remarkable views from the highest point of Mount Kenya. After the summit experience, descend using the established climbing and abseiling systems, returning to Shipton’s Camp, subject to weather, climbing pace and route conditions.

days.label: Day 06
days.title: Weather Contingency and Recovery Day – Shipton’s Camp
paragraphs: Keep this day available as a weather contingency for the Batian technical climb. If the summit attempt has been completed successfully on Day 5, use the day for recovery and additional acclimatisation at Shipton’s Camp.
If weather or climbing conditions prevented the previous day’s attempt, the technical guide will assess whether another summit attempt is safe and feasible.

days.label: Day 07
days.title: Shipton’s Camp – Old Moses Camp
paragraphs: After breakfast, begin descending through the scenic Mackinder Valley towards Old Moses Camp. Enjoy the changing mountain scenery as you leave the alpine moorland and gradually descend to lower elevations.

days.label: Day 08
days.title: Old Moses Camp – Sirimon Gate – Nanyuki
paragraphs: Complete the final descent to Sirimon Gate, where your vehicle will be waiting. Meet your transfer team and return to Nanyuki, marking the end of your Mount Kenya Batian technical climbing expedition.
